title: Purchase and install of wall-attached telescopic bleacher system and removal of existing bleachers
description: Amendment to solictation FA813626Q0011: This solicitation is hereby amended to revise the product description from brand-name-only requirement to brand-name-or-equal requirement. 1. Products other than the specified brand name may be offered provided the proposed product meets or exceeds all stated salient physical. functional, and performance charachteristics outlined in the updated Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors proposing an equal product must identify the manufacturer of proposed product and shall provide suffient descriptive literature, specifications and other technical information neccessary for the Governmenrt to determine whether the proposed product meets the stated requirements. 2. The previously posted Statement of Need (SON) has been replaced by the Statement of Work (SOW). The SOW is amended to revise the Government's requirements from brand-name to brand-name or equal. The revision permits products manufactured by sources other than the originally specified manufacturer, provided the proposed product satisfies the Government's stated minimum requirements. 3. The previously applicable Brand Name Justification, supporting the brand-name-only requirement identified in the original solicitation is no longer applicable due to the revision of the governements requirement, and that document has therefore been removed from this solicitation. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ The response deadline for this solicitation is 14 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. A site visit will be offered (optional) on 1 September 2026 so vendors can ensure accurate measurements. Questions are due 3 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. All interested parties should contact Lauren Rodgers, lauren.rodgers.5@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer MSgt Kristoforus Wenas, kristoforus.wenas.1@us.af.mil to schedule site visit. This RFQ is being issued on SAM.gov as a small business set aside. Purchase is required to satisfy Youth Center seating- � The current bleachers were installed 25 years ago and have reached the end of their service life. Replacement is necessary to ensure continued safety, reliability for all Youth Center spectators. The vendor will provide MAXAM telescopic bleachers manufactured by Hussey Seating Company, or equivelant, that will perform full installation of the system. The scope of work includes demolition and removal of the existing bleacher system. The new bleachers will be attached to the wall and designed to retract to extend maximum available floor space. System Classification � Brand & Model: Hussey Seating Company MAXAM Telescopic Series (or approved equivalent meeting identical dimensional and safety tolerances). � Design: Wall-attached, manually operated, multi-tier retractable spectator seating system designed specifically for indoor gymnasium environments. Physical Dimensions � Installed Length: Approximately 45 feet (45' total continuous length). � Fully Deployed Depth: Maximum 9 feet, 1 inch (9' 1") from the mounting wall. � Row Quantity & Spacing: 5 rows (tiers) of seating with a standard 22-inch to 24-inch row spacing to ensure adequate legroom and egress. Material & Construction � Understructure Frame: Heavy-duty, high-tensile structural steel shapes forming a rigid, self-supporting understructure, finished with a corrosion-resistant black powder coat. � Decks & Under-decking: Minimum 5/8-inch exterior-grade plywood panels with a durable, non-slip textured poly-wear surface overlay. � Seating Type: CourtSide collection (or equivelant) contoured HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) seats, 10-inch (254 mm) depth, featuring an anatomical curved design with a front "waterfall" edge to alleviate thigh pressure. Demolition & Site Prep � Complete demolition and removal of existing 25-year-old bleachers with zero damage to surrounding walls, gym floor, or utility lines. � 100% damage-free. Any accidental damage must be repaired/restored to original condition at contractor expense within 5 business days. � 100% Inspection by COR and Youth Center Facility Manager. Operational Method � Operation: Manual operation utilizing a high-efficiency pull-handle/draw-bar system. � Tracking: Must feature self-supporting first-row wheels and structural guide tracks to allow smooth, single-operator extension and retraction without binding. � Operational Training: Provide comprehensive, on-site operational and safety training to at least five (5) designated Youth Center staff members. Accessibility Compliance (ADA) � Wheelchair Spaces: Minimum of four (4) integrated, ADA-compliant wheelchair seating locations recovered within the footprint. � Companion Seating: Adjacent companion seating structurally integrated as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the International Building Code (IBC). Safety & Egress Features � Aisle Handrails: Center-aisle, self-storing, or removable structural steel handrails with round profiles, finished in high-visibility safety colors. � End Rails (Guardrails): Full-height steel guardrails at both open ends of the bleacher system, meeting a minimum lateral load requirement of 50 lbs/ft at the top rail. � Locking Mechanisms: Automatic mechanical tier locks that securely lock each row in the fully extended position to prevent accidental retraction during occupancy. Structural Load Standards � Compliance: Must conform to IBC (International Building Code) and ICC 300 (Standard for Bleachers, Folding and Telescopic Seating, and Grandstands) load ratings. � Active Live Load: Minimum 120 lbs/sq ft active horizontal framework capacity. � Sway Load: 24 lbs/linear ft parallel to seats; 10 lbs/linear ft perpendicular to seats. Execution & Safety Certification � Installation: Must be executed by a factory-certified installer. � Testing: Installer must conduct a formal structural and operational safety test prior to government acceptance. ***Additional requirements listed in attached SOW. Delivery/Services Required: The contractor shall be responsible for all freight and shipping costs to provide FOB Destination inside delivery to Tinker AFB, Oklahoma 73145. Delivery is required 60 days After Receipt of Order (ARO). Eligibility: The applicable NAICS Code for this requirement is 337127. The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this effort is 7195. This NAICS is the only applicable NAICS for this effort. To be considered for this award, contractor must have this NAICS on their profile. If it is not on contractor profile, request it to be added. In order to make a determination for a amall business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications and ability to perform in accordance with the Limitations on Subcontracting clause (FAR 52.219-14). Producuct Service Code: 7195 Pricing Arrangement: Firm Fixed Price

title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE:Law Manager Software License, Maintenance, and Technical Support Services
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & STATUTORY AUTHORITY The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Headquarters Contract Division 4 (CG-HCA-COCO-41), on behalf of the Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD), intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with Mitratech, located in Conshohocken, PA. The proposed contract action is to acquire proprietary software licenses, custom support services, ongoing maintenance, and upgrades for the Law Manager software application. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the statutory authority of: 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 253(c)(1), as implemented by FAR Subpart 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii): "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. 2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The USCG Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD) has a continuous, mission-critical requirement to obtain technical support services, maintenance support, software upgrades, and application modifications for the Law Manager software. Law Manager serves as the primary system of record and workload repository for approximately 300+ Coast Guard Legal Program personnel across Coast Guard Headquarters, ten District legal offices, several base legal offices, the Office of Physical Disability Evaluations, and their respective clients. Key System Specifications & Structure The Law Manager system comprises six main notebooks/tabs used for tracking, docketing, and case management across all USCG legal practice areas: Entity: Tracks units and individuals associated with cases (witnesses, counsel, judges, experts, plaintiffs, defendants). Matter: Handles legal assistance files and general legal inquiries. Military Justice: Manages military justice actions (e.g., courts-martial) and calculates the Speedy Trial Clock fields based on charges and calendars. Physical Disability (PDES): Evaluates cases for personnel seeking disability benefits. Regulations: Tracks the drafting, clearance, and review of regulatory documents. Claims/Litigation: Tracks affirmative and defensive claims and litigation for or against the USCG. The software is accessed via both a heavy client-installed application (for bulk data entry and speed) and a secure web application (primarily for reservists and personnel outside the Coast Guard Data Network). Scope of Work & Deliverables The contractor will be responsible for the following core tasks: Ongoing Maintenance & Technical Support: Deliver modified production code, technical documentation, operational procedures, and product updates to ensure zero-error system performance during normal business hours. System Configuration & Custom Modifications: Assist with minor configuration changes (e.g., adding/removing fields, re-labeling existing fields, enhancing functionality as the application-image evolves). Software Upgrades & Security Patches: Provide and assist in the installation of all software upgrades, tool sets, and database environment updates. Testing: Develop Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT) plans and run verification test scripts with mock data for adding, updating, finding, and deleting records within all system notebooks. Optional Report Writing Tool (Section 2.3.1): Acquire a fully compatible, vendor-supported ad hoc report writing and querying tool. Optional Support Hours (Section 2.3.2): Secure up to 1,000 hours of custom technical support to execute USCG-specific modifications. 3. ESTIMATED VALUE & PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The Government anticipates awarding a Fixed Price contract with an estimated total value of $828,845 covering a one (1) year base period and four (4) consecutive one-year option periods: Base Year Period of Performance Start Date: September 30, 2026 End Date September 29, 2027 Option Year 1 September 30, 2027- September 29, 2028 Option Year 2 September 30, 2028- September 29, 2029 Option Year 3 September 30, 2029- September 29, 2030 Option Year 4 September 30, 2030- September 29, 2031 4. SOLE SOURCE DETERMINATION RATIONALE The Law Manager application is a highly customized, proprietary commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software system. Mitratech is the developer, sole intellectual property owner, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of Law Manager. The justification for sole-source award to Mitratech is based on the following critical technical factors: Access to Source Code & Engineers: Mitratech has sole access to the software engineers who created Law Manager and is the only entity that can resolve deep-level software bugs or configure the application to integrate smoothly with the Coast Guard's standard operating image. Mitratech personnel possess exclusive access to the proprietary source code for current and future releases. Proprietary Technical Documentation: Mitratech personnel utilize proprietary technical documentation and receive unique, specialized internal training/briefings directly from the Law Manager product development team that are unavailable to any third party. Restricted Licensing Policy: Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements for upgrades. No other vendor in the market owns the rights or data to Thomson Elite�s original source code or Mitratech's proprietary assets. Mission Criticality: This software is vital to daily USCG legal operations. Specifically, attorneys must perform immediate, reliable conflict-of-interest checks within the Law Manager database before consulting with clients. It is also the sole vehicle for workload metrics and resource allocation reporting at Coast Guard Headquarters. Significant Cost & Legacy History: In 1999, the Coast Guard abandoned its efforts to migrate mission-critical applications from legacy CTOS to Windows due to database porting failures. After a rigorous selection process, the USCG selected and deployed Law Manager in 2001. A replacement effort would lead to a massive duplication of costs (including a minimum of $828,845 in support, plus undocumented system engineering, data migration, and extensive staff retraining costs) and severe, unacceptable operational disruptions that are impossible to recover through competition. 5. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS Interested firms who believe they can fully meet the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement. Because Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements or share its proprietary source code, any responding firm must provide clear, undeniable written proof of their legal right, authorized partner status, and independent capability to modify and upgrade the Law Manager application without voiding current licensing, warranties, or security configurations. At a minimum, responses must include: Company Profile: Name, physical address, Point of Contact (POC), UEI number, Cage Code, and business size under NAICS 541519. Authorized Documentation: Written authorization directly from the OEM (Mitratech) confirming the respondent has full access to, and authority to edit, the proprietary source code and technical documentation. Staffing Qualifications: Demonstration of qualified personnel (e.g., Project Manager) available during standard business hours (0800�1600 EST) to meet all SOW requirements. Technical Qualifications: A detailed description of the firm's experience supporting Law Manager platforms within the federal sector. Staffing Capabilities: Evidence of qualified personnel (such as a Project Manager meeting the SOW standard of M-F, 0800-1600 EST availability) capable of managing the transition, Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT), and custom programming requirements. Capability statements must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed below no later than September 14, 2026, 3:00 PM EST.

title: Purchase and install of Hussy Seating Maxim wall-attached telescopic bleacher system and removal of existing bleachers
description: The response deadline for this solicitation is 14 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. A site visit will be offered (optional) on 1 September 2026 so vendors can ensure accurate measurements. Questions are due 3 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST. All interested parties should contact Lauren Rodgers, lauren.rodgers.5@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer MSgt Kristoforus Wenas, kristoforus.wenas.1@us.af.mil to schedule site visit. This RFQ is being issued on SAM.gov as a small business set aside. Purchase is required to satisfy Youth Center seating- � The current bleachers were installed 25 years ago and have reached the end of their service life. Replacement is necessary to ensure continued safety, reliability for all Youth Center spectators. The vendor will provide MAXAM telescopic bleachers manufactured by Hussey Seating Company that will perform full installation of the system. The scope of work includes demolition and removal of the existing bleacher system. The new bleachers will be attached to the wall and designed to retract to extend maximum available floor space. System Classification � Brand & Model: Hussey Seating Company MAXAM Telescopic Series (or approved equivalent meeting identical dimensional and safety tolerances). � Design: Wall-attached, manually operated, multi-tier retractable spectator seating system designed specifically for indoor gymnasium environments. Physical Dimensions � Installed Length: Approximately 45 feet (45' total continuous length). � Fully Deployed Depth: Maximum 9 feet, 1 inch (9' 1") from the mounting wall. � Row Quantity & Spacing: 5 rows (tiers) of seating with a standard 22-inch to 24-inch row spacing to ensure adequate legroom and egress. Material & Construction � Understructure Frame: Heavy-duty, high-tensile structural steel shapes forming a rigid, self-supporting understructure, finished with a corrosion-resistant black powder coat. � Decks & Under-decking: Minimum 5/8-inch exterior-grade plywood panels with a durable, non-slip textured poly-wear surface overlay. � Seating Type: CourtSide collection contoured HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) seats, 10-inch (254 mm) depth, featuring an anatomical curved design with a front "waterfall" edge to alleviate thigh pressure. Demolition & Site Prep � Complete demolition and removal of existing 25-year-old bleachers with zero damage to surrounding walls, gym floor, or utility lines. � 100% damage-free. Any accidental damage must be repaired/restored to original condition at contractor expense within 5 business days. � 100% Inspection by COR and Youth Center Facility Manager. Operational Method � Operation: Manual operation utilizing a high-efficiency pull-handle/draw-bar system. � Tracking: Must feature self-supporting first-row wheels and structural guide tracks to allow smooth, single-operator extension and retraction without binding. � Operational Training: Provide comprehensive, on-site operational and safety training to at least five (5) designated Youth Center staff members. Accessibility Compliance (ADA) � Wheelchair Spaces: Minimum of four (4) integrated, ADA-compliant wheelchair seating locations recovered within the footprint. � Companion Seating: Adjacent companion seating structurally integrated as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the International Building Code (IBC). Safety & Egress Features � Aisle Handrails: Center-aisle, self-storing, or removable structural steel handrails with round profiles, finished in high-visibility safety colors. � End Rails (Guardrails): Full-height steel guardrails at both open ends of the bleacher system, meeting a minimum lateral load requirement of 50 lbs/ft at the top rail. � Locking Mechanisms: Automatic mechanical tier locks that securely lock each row in the fully extended position to prevent accidental retraction during occupancy. Structural Load Standards � Compliance: Must conform to IBC (International Building Code) and ICC 300 (Standard for Bleachers, Folding and Telescopic Seating, and Grandstands) load ratings. � Active Live Load: Minimum 120 lbs/sq ft active horizontal framework capacity. � Sway Load: 24 lbs/linear ft parallel to seats; 10 lbs/linear ft perpendicular to seats. Execution & Safety Certification � Installation: Must be executed by a factory-certified installer. � Testing: Installer must conduct a formal structural and operational safety test prior to government acceptance. ***Additional requirements listed in attached SON. Delivery/Services Required: The contractor shall be responsible for all freight and shipping costs to provide FOB Destination inside delivery to Tinker AFB, Oklahoma 73145. Delivery is required 60 days After Receipt of Order (ARO). Eligibility: The applicable NAICS Code for this requirement is 337127. The Product/Service Code (PSC) for this effort is 7195. This NAICS is the only applicable NAICS for this effort. To be considered for this award, contractor must have this NAICS on their profile. If it is not on contractor profile, request it to be added. title: Petroleum Quality Analysis System - Enhanced (PQAS-E) Analytical Lab Equipment Upgrades
description: The Government is issuing this Sources Sought notice as part of a market research effort to identify capable sources that can supply replacement analytical instrumentation for the Petroleum Quality Analysis System-Enhanced (PQAS-E) utilized by the 209th Aviation Support Battalion (209th ASB), 25th Combat Aviation Brigade (25th CAB). The PQAS-E is a self-contained, mobile fuel laboratory designed to test and measure the quality of kerosene-based military mobility fuels and aviation turbine fuels in accordance with Military Standard 3004C (MIL-STD-3004C). The required hardware must fit within the physical dimensions, power constraints, and software parameters of the existing PQAS-E Shelter System and Computer Data Acquisition (CDA) subsystem. The Government�s primary objective through this market research is to determine whether a single vendor is capable of providing the complete PQAS-E requirement, including all required parts, equipment, components, accessories, and incidental support services. Vendors are requested to clearly state whether they can satisfy the entire requirement. If unable to provide the full requirement, vendors shall identify with specificity the exact items, components, and/or services they are able to furnish.

title: Anchorage Air Force Reserve Recruiting Office
description: The Government currently occupies office and related space under a lease that will be expiring and will consider alternative space if economically advantageous. The Government is seeking retail space consisting of approximately 1190 Square feet of space, and parking for up to three (3) government vehicles (sign designated preferred) for an Armed Forces Recruiting Office. The lease shall be a fully-serviced lease for a term of five (5) years, with the Government having termination rights. All offers must be within the Delineated Area set forth below (Anchorage, Alaska). Offers to include base rent, CAM, utilities, janitorial, and parking. If awarded to a new location, this office would be relocated immediately upon completion of construction of office space to accommodate all requirements pertaining to the FY26 Construction Specifications for production offices with the lease start date commencing upon acceptance of space by the government (see attached Construction Specifications.) In making this determination, the Government will consider, among other things, the availability of alternate space that potentially can satisfy the Government�s requirements and is economically advantageous, as well as costs likely to be incurred through relocation. The requirements for consideration of award will entail a complete bid that consists of the following criteria at a minimum: Space must meet established square footage requirements and be within the delineated area (see attached delineated area.) Acceptance and use of government lease, with no changes to the standard language, clauses or conditions within the lease as designated by the Government (see attached Standard Lease Template and General Clauses.) Competitive rates of base cost per square feet for annual rent (see attached Proposal to Lease Form). Include a breakout of operation expenses including janitorial services costs based on the attach Janitorial Specifications. All costs and materials affiliated to meet the requirements of the Construction Specifications (including all safety and security enhancement�s) will be considered Tenant Improvements with no reimbursement from the Government upon completion of the construction or through amortization within the lease. Lease will be awarded to the most economically advantageous bid which provides best value to the Government. Evaluation criteria to include, but not limited to, meets recruiting mission requirements, location, lessor past performance (if applicable), site visibility, and pricing consistent with comparable sites in the local area. Offered space must meet the Governments requirements per the terms of the Government Lease. Interested respondents may include building owners and representatives with the exclusive right to represent the building owners. Representatives of building owners must include the exclusivity grating the exclusive right to represent the building owner with their response to the advertisement. Offers will need to include a completed Rental Proposal Worksheet, proof of registration in www.sam.gov (i.e. active CAGE code), a proposed floor plan and the construction bids for build-out meeting the construction specifications. Attached is a copy of the Rental Proposal Worksheet, lease document, the General Clauses, Proposal to Lease Space, Construction Specifications, Construction Bid Proposal Worksheet, Janitorial Specifications, Agency Agreement, and a floor plan template. Please review all documents carefully and make sure that you agree to the terms presented. The government lease and the general conditions are standard and are for the most part is not negotiable and must be accepted as written and shown on the attached file. Review the construction specifications completely as they stipulate additional lessor responsibilities. Three (3) construction bids for the build-out are requested. After a bid is accepted, no change orders are authorized, so bids need to be accurate and complete (including all taxes and fees). Special attention should be given to security requirements (video entry control system, closed circuit television system and video recording, dual roller shades on exterior windows, fixed panel shade on exterior entry door and peep hole in secondary exit, perforated window wrap), fragmentation film on exterior windows/glass doors, telecommunication wiring requirements, addition of water fountain, signage, paint, wall graphics, phone jacks, electrical outlets and spec'd carpet squares. These are items that can add a significant cost and may be overlooked in the bid process; however, all items in the specifications need to be followed, even if code does not require the item (i.e. smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, etc.). Bids shall include any tear down/haul away expenses. Initial offers are due no later than close of business on 14 September 2026. After the receipt of initial offers, the named Realty Specialist or other authorized representative will conduct negotiation on behalf of the Government. Verbal or written negotiations will be conducted with Offerors that are within the competitive range. The competitive range, which will be established by the Realty Specialist, will be based on the lease cost and other award factors stated in this solicitation. All Offerors will be included that have a reasonable chance of being selected. Negotiations are considered closed at the due date and time of best and final offers.

title: Vocational Training Programs
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part RFO FAR part 12.202. This announcement constitutes the solicitation only. Quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Mission Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington currently intends to award a contract for Education and Vocational Training for prisoners confined at the Northwestern Joint Regional Correctional Facility (NWJRCF). The NWJRCF prison inmate population is located at 20000 Alder Rd, Joint Base Lewis-McChord, WA 98433. The contractor shall provide instructors and state approved curriculum for a Vocational Training Program to provide prisoners with the knowledge and skills for future employment, preparation for certification, degrees, and licensure. The NWJRCF is a medium security correctional facility which houses military prisoners with sentences up to 10 years. The mission of the NWJRCF is to provide custody/control, education, and vocational opportunities as well as behavioral/mental health programs to prisoners to assist their transition back into the civilian community or return to duty. The NWJRCF houses prisoners in the military correctional system. Prisoners who demonstrate good behavior, desire to learn, who qualify after screening, and with enough time remaining in their sentences may be enrolled in vocational education programs. The prisoners work toward good conduct time and are kept gainfully employed by learning new skills that in turn prepare them for work upon release. All duties shall be performed in accordance with standards and methods generally accepted within industry and in compliance with all Federal and State policies and regulations. The U.S. Government highly encourages all interested businesses (large and small) to respond to this RFQ.

title: Chemistry Research for the Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT)
description: The mission of National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) is to discover how the environment affects people to promote healthier lives. The Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) is an intramural division at NIEHS, and DTT scientists use a variety of traditional and cutting-edge approaches to better understand how factors in our environment may impact our health. One of DTT's goals is to lead the transformation of toxicology through the development and application of innovative tools and strategies. This contract will provide required chemistry research at each step of the DTT toxicological evaluation process. This acquisition is to conduct Chemistry Research for NIEHS, Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) and National Toxicology Program (NTP). The type and extent of chemistry research support provided will be specific to DTT and NTP research needs. Program management procedures and chemistry technical activities will be provided under eight (8) Functional Areas: Logistics and Handling, Characterization, Formulation, Biosample Analysis, Special Studies, Animal Studies, Omics and In Vitro Assays. Specifications for the Conduct of Chemistry Activities for Toxicology Research Performed by the Division of Translational Toxicology at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (DTT Chemistry Specifications): https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/data/research/chemistry/rfp

A detailed description can be located in the associated Performance Work Statement (PWS). 4a) Childcare Services: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, and supplies to supervise and care for approximately 25 children (estimated 15 children aged 0-5; 10 youth aged 6-17) on Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 0600 to 1700. title: Chemistry Research for the Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT)
description: The mission of National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) is to discover how the environment affects people to promote healthier lives. The Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) is an intramural division at NIEHS, and DTT scientists use a variety of traditional and cutting-edge approaches to better understand how factors in our environment may impact our health. One of DTT's goals is to lead the transformation of toxicology through the development and application of innovative tools and strategies. This contract will provide required chemistry research at each step of the DTT toxicological evaluation process. This acquisition is to conduct Chemistry Research for NIEHS, Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT) and National Toxicology Program (NTP). The type and extent of chemistry research support provided will be specific to DTT and NTP research needs. Program management procedures and chemistry technical activities will be provided under eight (8) Functional Areas: Logistics and Handling, Characterization, Formulation, Biosample Analysis, Special Studies, Animal Studies, Omics and In Vitro Assays. Specifications for the Conduct of Chemistry Activities for Toxicology Research Performed by the Division of Translational Toxicology at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (DTT Chemistry Specifications): https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/data/research/chemistry/rfp

title: National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) Survey and Evaluation
description: This combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services is issued in accordance with RFO Part 5 and RFO 12.202 to acquire non-personal services for the inventory and evaluation of archaeological sites and structures for listing in the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) at Fort Campbell, KY. In accordance with Sections 106 and 110 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) of 1966 and implementing regulations at 36 CFR Part 800, the Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, and transportation necessary to perform Phase I Archaeological site detection surveys, Phase II Archaeological site evaluations, and Architectural/Structural NRHP eligibility evaluations in strict accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Completion of these identification and evaluation surveys is essential to supporting military readiness by resolving current land-use and construction restrictions across the installation. This is a non-personal services contract where the Government shall exercise no supervision or control over contract personnel, who shall be accountable solely to the Contractor. title: Spectroradiometer With Specialized Lens for Characterizing Head Mounted Displays
description: Notice of Combined Synopsis/Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Background: The procurement is to support regulatory science tools development for the Interventional, Radiological Imaging and Visualization program. Developing measurement methodologies for technical performance is critical for consistent evaluation of image visualization on head mounted displays. Specifically, the procurement is for a spectroradiometer to precisely measure and evaluate the spectrum and color performance of image quality of augmented and virtual reality head mounted displays that are increasingly being incorporated in medical devices across the Office of Product Evaluation and Quality (OPEQ). The quantitative measurements from the spectroradiometer will allow for developing image quality regulatory science tools for a wider range image quality parameters across the full range of device types, opposed to only measuring luminance values. The specialized lens assembly on the spectroradiometer mimics the human visual system, which is critical for determining the image quality seen by the user. This will align the Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL) instrumentation with FDA recognized standards, such as the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), for head mounted displays, which is essential for the OSEL mission of developing regulatory science tools. Minimum Performance Requirements: Item 1: Spectroradiometer Optical Specifications: � Wavelength range: at least 380-780 nm � Sensor size: at least 512 elements � Detector type for spectroradiometer: back-thinned and cooled CCD � Spectral resolution/Spectral bandwidth: < 5 nm, option for variable resolution preferable � Datapoint interval/Spectral reporting: 1 nm or less � Digital resolution: 16 bits Performance Specifications: � Wavelength accuracy: < 0.5 nm � Luminance accuracy: < +/- 3% � Integration time range: minimum 10 ms to 60 seconds � Stray light: less than 0.06% � Polarization error: less than 2% � Sensitivity: at least 5*10^-5 cd/m2 with a 2 degrees internal aperture measuring Illuminant A � Color accuracy (x,y): less than +/- 0.002 � Color repeatability (x,y): less than +/- 0.0005 Hardware Features � Variable internal aperture diameters: 2 degrees, 1 degree, and 0.1-0.25 degrees � Integrated neutral density filter: ND1 or ND2 � Communication: USB � Physical dimension: less than 20 cm x 36 cm x 36 cm � Weight: < 10 kg Item 2: Specialized lens for measuring near eye displays, including augmented and virtual reality displays The contractor shall provide a specialized lens optimized for measuring augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) displays with the following specifications: � Focal length: 30-50 mm � Front entrance pupil design with a fixed pupil with a diameter between 3 mm and 5 mm � Adjustable focus range: at least 300 mm to infinity � Luminance accuracy: < +/- 3% Item 3: Software The contractor shall provide software with the following capabilities: Core Functions: � Control spectroradiometer operations � Acquire measurements � Display spectrum and color measurements � Analyze measurement data Data Export: � Export raw data in Excel, ASCII, or equivalent formats Integration: � Software Development Kits (SDKs) or command line support for third-party software control � Compatible with Python and MATLAB � Compatible with Windows 10 Operating System or later versions � Compatible with Windows 10, Windows 11, or Linux Operating System Deliverables: The Contractor shall deliver the item and quantities ordered within 60 days of award. The Contractor shall deliver the following items and quantities ordered, all, or none: � Spectroradiometer system (Item 1) - fully calibrated and tested � Specialized lens for near-eye displays (Item 2) � Control and analysis software (Item 3) with installation media and documentation � Calibration certificate(s) or test report(s) � User manuals and technical documentation for all equipment � Software documentation including SDK/API documentation Place of Supply Delivery and Place of Performance: The equipment should be complete with all accessories and software necessary to work and to be delivered to: Attention: Yasaman Ardeshirpour U.S. Food and Drug Administration White Oak Building 62 Room 1112 10903 New Hampshire Ave, Silver Spring, MD 20993-0002 Period of Performance: 12-month Base Year and Four, 12-month Option Years commencing upon date of award. Please see the attached Statement of Work and corresponding ancillary documents for review and consideration. Quotes are due by email on or before September 14, 2026, by 4:00 P.M. (Eastern Standard Time) and should be sent to brandon.rafus@fda.hhs.gov.

title: Spectroradiometer with specialized lens for characterizing head mounted displays
description: Notice of Combined Synopsis/Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Background: The procurement is to support regulatory science tools development for the Interventional, Radiological Imaging and Visualization program. Developing measurement methodologies for technical performance is critical for consistent evaluation of image visualization on head mounted displays. Specifically, the procurement is for a spectroradiometer to precisely measure and evaluate the spectrum and color performance of image quality of augmented and virtual reality head mounted displays that are increasingly being incorporated in medical devices across the Office of Product Evaluation and Quality (OPEQ). The quantitative measurements from the spectroradiometer will allow for developing image quality regulatory science tools for a wider range image quality parameters across the full range of device types, opposed to only measuring luminance values. The specialized lens assembly on the spectroradiometer mimics the human visual system, which is critical for determining the image quality seen by the user. This will align the Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL) instrumentation with FDA recognized standards, such as the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), for head mounted displays, which is essential for the OSEL mission of developing regulatory science tools. Minimum Performance Requirements: Item 1: Spectroradiometer Optical Specifications: � Wavelength range: at least 380-780 nm � Sensor size: at least 512 elements � Detector type for spectroradiometer: back-thinned and cooled CCD � Spectral resolution/Spectral bandwidth: < 5 nm, option for variable resolution preferable � Datapoint interval/Spectral reporting: 1 nm or less � Digital resolution: 16 bits Performance Specifications: � Wavelength accuracy: < 0.5 nm � Luminance accuracy: < +/- 3% � Integration time range: minimum 10 ms to 60 seconds � Stray light: less than 0.06% � Polarization error: less than 2% � Sensitivity: at least 5*10^-5 cd/m2 with a 2 degrees internal aperture measuring Illuminant A � Color accuracy (x,y): less than +/- 0.002 � Color repeatability (x,y): less than +/- 0.0005 Hardware Features � Variable internal aperture diameters: 2 degrees, 1 degree, and 0.1-0.25 degrees � Integrated neutral density filter: ND1 or ND2 � Communication: USB � Physical dimension: less than 20 cm x 36 cm x 36 cm � Weight: < 10 kg Item 2: Specialized lens for measuring near eye displays, including augmented and virtual reality displays The contractor shall provide a specialized lens optimized for measuring augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) displays with the following specifications: � Focal length: 30-50 mm � Front entrance pupil design with a fixed pupil with a diameter between 3 mm and 5 mm � Adjustable focus range: at least 300 mm to infinity � Luminance accuracy: < +/- 3% Item 3: Software The contractor shall provide software with the following capabilities: Core Functions: � Control spectroradiometer operations � Acquire measurements � Display spectrum and color measurements � Analyze measurement data Data Export: � Export raw data in Excel, ASCII, or equivalent formats Integration: � Software Development Kits (SDKs) or command line support for third-party software control � Compatible with Python and MATLAB � Compatible with Windows 10 Operating System or later versions � Compatible with Windows 10, Windows 11, or Linux Operating System Deliverables: The Contractor shall deliver the item and quantities ordered within 60 days of award. The Contractor shall deliver the following items and quantities ordered, all, or none: � Spectroradiometer system (Item 1) - fully calibrated and tested � Specialized lens for near-eye displays (Item 2) � Control and analysis software (Item 3) with installation media and documentation � Calibration certificate(s) or test report(s) � User manuals and technical documentation for all equipment � Software documentation including SDK/API documentation Place of Supply Delivery and Place of Performance: The equipment should be complete with all accessories and software necessary to work and to be delivered to: Attention: Yasaman Ardeshirpour U.S. Food and Drug Administration White Oak Building 62 Room 1112 10903 New Hampshire Ave, Silver Spring, MD 20993-0002 Period of Performance: 12-month Base Year and Four, 12-month Option Years commencing upon date of award. Completion of these identification and evaluation surveys is essential to supporting military readiness by resolving current land-use and construction restrictions across the installation. This is a non-personal services contract where the Government shall exercise no supervision or control over contract personnel, who shall be accountable solely to the Contractor. Email questions regarding this synopsis/solicitation to the Contract Specialist, SSG Denver S, Cristello, denver.s.cristello.mil@army.mil and Contracting Officer, SFC Catherine R. Mckinney, catherine.r.mckinney.mil@army.mil. The Government will answer all questions provided that the questions are received by 08 September 2026 at 12:00 PM CT.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. title: Trailer - Mounted Diesel Engine Driven (DED) Welder
description: The Trailer-Mounted 400 AMP Diesel Engine Driven (DED) Welder is designed to replace legacy 300 AMP systems currently in use across expeditionary forces TOAs that have reached the end of their service life. This welder provides a reliable and mobile welding solution for use in austere, forward-deployed environments where shore power is not available or practical. The system is towable by organic assets and fully transportable by air and surface across all standard DoD platforms, ensuring flexibility across diverse mission profiles. Operating on NATO fuels, the welder delivers consistent performance in all climates and supports both Civil Engineer Support Equipment repair and general construction tasks. Its configuration ensures seamless integration into expeditionary operations while maintaining continuity in support and logistics structures.

Scope: This solicitation is for the procurement of aircraft components that are determined to be commercial items in accordance with FAR 2.101 and FAR Part12. Offerors shall provide components that are currently in production and offered in the commercial marketplace, or that have been offered for sale, lease, or license to the general public or non-governmental entities. 2. Applicable Regulations: This acquisition shall be conducted in accordance with: FAR Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR Part 13/15, as applicable (based on dollar value or acquisition method) DFARS 212, as applicable for Department of Defense requirements 3. Commercial Item Determination: Offerors shall provide documentation supporting the commerciality of the offered item(s), which may include: Commercial product descriptions and technical specifications Sales history or catalog pricing Copies of sales invoices or redacted purchase orders to non-government customers Published price lists or marketing materials 4. Technical Requirements Offered components must meet the Government's form, fit, and function requirements. Submissions must include datasheets, drawings, or specifications that demonstrate compliance with performance requirements outlined in the technical description. Any deviation from the stated technical requirements must be clearly nd is in a condition for safe operation (Block 11a). 5. Certification and Traceability Vendors must certify that all components are new, unused, and conform to commercial standards. Traceability documentation shall be provided to verify the supply chain from the original manufacturer to the vendor. Documentation may include FAA Form 8130-3, Certificate of Conformance, Part Manufacturer Approval (PMA) Documentation or equivalent. Authorized Release Certificate Requirement - FAA Form 8130-3 All components delivered under this contract shall be accompanied by a properlyexecuted FAA Form 8130-3 Authorized Release Certificate. For new (spare) components, the 8130-3 shall be issued by an FAA-approved production approval holder (PAH) and certify that the item conforms to FAA-approved design data and is in a condition for safe operation (Block 11a). The 8130-3 must: Include the correct part number, serial number (if applicable), and contract/purchase order number and Be completed legibly and in accordancewith current FAA guidance (e.g., FAA Order 8130.21 series) 6. Delivery All shipments must be traceable and include packing lists identifying part number, nomenclature, quantity, and contract number. 7. Warranty and Support A standard commercial warranty must be provided. Warranty terms must be at least equal to those provided to the vendor's commercial customers and must include workmanship and replacement parts. Technical support must be available during the warranty period. 8. Marking and Labeling Components must be labeled with the part number, manufacturer's name or CAGE code, and lot or serial number (if applicable). 9. Contract Data Requirements No military-unique Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) will apply unless explicitly identified. Commercial documentation shall suffice unless otherwise negotiated. This Solicitation is being issued under EAF Authority formally known as SEPA. For Critical Safety Items (CSI), DFARS clause 252.209-7010, Identification of Critical Safety Items, is incorporated by reference. As applicable, DFARS clause 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, is incorporated by reference. Drawings are not available for this Request for Quote. Offerors are advised that offers received from sources which are not government-approved sources of supply will be deemed technically unacceptable, and therefore ineligible for award. Any distributors of approved sources MUST submit a copy of their authorized distributor letter, on the source letterhead, to the buyer point of contact indicated on the solicitation via email, at time of proposal submittal. All potential offers shall provide newly manufactured spares only. Refurbished, remanufactured, or repaired material will not be acceptable. Offers for such are ineligible for award. Per the PMA-290 IUID implementation plan, IUID is not required for commercial items because "Traceability of the 737NG commercial common and P-8A noncore items have been captured and accounted for as a part of the parent end item recorded in the DoD IUID Registry."

description: This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Government is seeking to identify Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE), and any other category of vendor capable of performing the below Indian Health Service (IHS) requirement. Any vendor responding to this notice should submit their capability statement as well as the Buy Indian Act Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form (attached). Consistent with the revised Buy Indian Act, HHS/IHS adopted the definition of an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) set forth in 48 CFR 1480.201. This definition includes the following requirement, amongst others: �the Indians or Indian Tribes must, together, receive at least a majority of the earnings from the contract.� Instructions for submission are outlined further below. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT NAICS Code: 621210 Small Business Size Standard: $9 million in average annual receipts Estimated Period of Performance: Three (3) months from date of award, with a possible option to extend services for up to six (6) months in accordance with FAR 52.217-8, to ensure continuity of care pending award of a planned follow-on long-term contract for the same requirement. Estimated Value: To be determined based on market research. 1. Purpose of Notice This Sources Sought Notice is issued in accordance with the Buy Indian Act, 25 U.S.C. � 47, and its implementing regulations, to conduct market research and determine the availability and interest of qualified Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) capable of providing the supplies/services described below. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submission of information does not guarantee that a solicitation for this requirement will be issued, nor does it obligate the Government to award any resulting contract. 2. Background / Requirement Description The Billings Area Indian Health Service (BAIHS), Blackfeet Service Unit (BFSU), provides comprehensive healthcare services to American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries residing on and near the Blackfeet Indian Reservation in Browning, Montana. The Blackfeet Community Hospital requires continued access to dental oral and maxillofacial surgery services to meet the clinical needs of its patient population. A draft Performance Work Statement is attached to this notice. 3. Anticipated Acquisition Strategy This requirement is subject to the Buy Indian Act order of precedence set forth at HHSAR 326.603-1. Respondents are requested to identify their status as an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) or Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE), if applicable. If the Government determines after market research that there is no reasonable expectation of obtaining two or more competitive offers from ISBEE/IEE concerns, the Contracting Officer may proceed under the deviation process at HHSAR 326.603-3. 4. Indian Economic Enterprise / Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise Requirements To be considered an IEE or ISBEE for purposes of this notice, an entity must meet the applicable definitions and ownership/control requirements set forth at 25 U.S.C. � 47 and HHSAR 326.601, including but not limited to: The combined Indian, Federally Recognized Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Corporation ownership of the enterprise constitutes not less than 51%; The Indian, Federal Recognized Indian Tribes, or Alaska Native Corporations must, together, receive at least 51% of the earnings from the contract; and The management and daily business operations must be controlled by one or more individuals who are Indians. Respondents claiming IEE or ISBEE status should identify their status clearly in their response and be prepared to provide supporting documentation upon request. 5. Information Requested Interested and qualified sources, particularly IEEs and ISBEEs, are requested to submit the following information: Company Information: Name, address, point of contact, phone number, email address, and UEI (Unique Entity Identifier). Business Status: Indicate whether your firm qualifies as an IEE, ISBEE, or other small business concern, and identify the specific socioeconomic certifications held (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB), if any. Capability Statement: A narrative not to exceed ten pages describing your firm's experience performing work of the same or similar scope, complexity and clinical setting as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), including at least two relevant past or current contracts, with the following for each: contract number, customer, dollar value, period of performance, and brief description of work performed. Bonding/Licensing (if applicable): Evidence of any required licenses, certifications, or bonding capacity relevant to the requirement. Teaming/Subcontracting: If your firm intends to team with or subcontract to another entity to meet the requirement, identify the proposed teaming partner(s) and the anticipated division of work. Statement of Interest: A brief statement confirming your firm's interest in and capability to compete for this requirement if a solicitation is issued. 6. Instructions for Submission All responses shall be submitted electronically to Prudence.YellowOwl@ihs.gov no later than September 14, 2026 at 2:30pm MT. Responses shall be limited to 10 pages, in PDF, 12-point font. Responses will not be returned and will not be publicly posted. All information marked as proprietary or confidential will be treated accordingly to the extent permitted by law. 7. Disclaimer This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or to award a contract. No entitlement to compensation shall arise as a result of a firm's submission of information in response to this notice or the Government's use of that information. Firms responding to this notice are solely responsible for all costs associated with their response. The Government reserves the right to consider a non-IEE/ISBEE small business or full-and-open acquisition strategy if market research indicates an insufficient number of interested and qualified IEEs/ISBEEs exist to reasonably expect competition.

Scope: This solicitation is for the procurement of aircraft components that are determined to be commercial items in accordance with FAR 2.101 and FAR Part12. Offerors shall provide components that are currently in production and offered in the commercial marketplace, or that have been offered for sale, lease, or license to the general public or non-governmental entities. 2. Applicable Regulations: This acquisition shall be conducted in accordance with: FAR Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR Part 13/15, as applicable (based on dollar value or acquisition method) DFARS 212, as applicable for Department of Defense requirements 3. Commercial Item Determination: Offerors shall provide documentation supporting the commerciality of the offered item(s), which may include: Commercial product descriptions and technical specifications Sales history or catalog pricing Copies of sales invoices or redacted purchase orders to non-government customers Published price lists or marketing materials 4. Technical Requirements Offered components must meet the Government's form, fit, and function requirements. Submissions must include datasheets, drawings, or specifications that demonstrate compliance with performance requirements outlined in the technical description. Any deviation from the stated technical requirements must be clearly identifiedand justified. 5. Certification and Traceability Vendors must certify that all components are new, unused, and conform to commercial standards. Traceability documentation shall be provided to verify the supply chain from the original manufacturer to the vendor. Documentation may include FAA Form 8130-3, Certificate of Conformance, Part Manufacturer Approval (PMA) Documentation or equivalent. Authorized Release Certificate Requirement - FAA Form 8130-3 All components delivered under this contract shall be accompanied by a properlyexecuted FAA Form 8130-3 Authorized Release Certificate. For new (spare) components, the 8130-3 shall be issued by an FAA-approved production approval holder (PAH) and certify that the item conforms to FAA-approved design data and is in a condition for safe operation (Block 11a). The 8130-3 must: Include the correct part number, serial number (if applicable), and contract/purchase order number and Be completed legibly and in accordancewith current FAA guidance (e.g., FAA Order 8130.21 series) 6. Delivery All shipments must be traceable and include packing lists identifying part number, nomenclature, quantity, and contract number. 7. Warranty and Support A standard commercial warranty must be provided. Warranty terms must be at least equal to those provided to the vendor's commercial customers and must include workmanship and replacement parts. Technical support must be available during the warranty period. 8. Marking and Labeling Components must be labeled with the part number, manufacturer's name or CAGE code, and lot or serial number (if applicable). 9. Contract Data Requirements No military-unique Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) will apply unless explicitly identified. Commercial documentation shall suffice unless otherwise negotiated. This Solicitation is being issued under EAF Authority formally known as SEPA. For Critical Safety Items (CSI), DFARS clause 252.209-7010, Identification of Critical Safety Items, is incorporated by reference. As applicable, DFARS clause 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, is incorporated by reference. Drawings are not available for this Request for Quote. Offerors are advised that offers received from sources which are not government-approved sources of supply will be deemed technically unacceptable, and therefore ineligible for award. Any distributors of approved sources MUST submit a copy of their authorized distributor letter, on the source letterhead, to the buyer point of contact indicated on the solicitation via email, at time of proposal submittal. description: AMENDMENT 0001: This amendment is issued to provide a response to an inquiry received regarding this Sources Sought Notice. All other terms, conditions, and requirements of the original notice remain unchanged. This notice does not constitute a solicitation and is issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with RFO 10.001. The Government will not accept unsolicited proposals or binding offers in response to this notice. Interested parties should continue to submit capability statements as outlined in the original notice by the response date indicated above. Question 1: Could you please confirm whether any additional documents, such as the proposed Oral Surgeon's resume/CV or credentialing documents, are required with the response at this stage? Answer 1: No. At this stage, no resume/CV for the proposed Oral Surgeon, nor any credentialing documentation (e.g., state license, DEA registration, board certification, malpractice history, or privileging records), is required to be submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice. At the Sources Sought stage, the Government is assessing general firm capability and experience, not evaluating specific personnel. Should a solicitation be issued, any personnel qualification requirements will be addressed in the solicitation's evaluation criteria. ----------------------------------------------------- This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Government is seeking to identify Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE), and any other category of vendor capable of performing the below Indian Health Service (IHS) requirement. Any vendor responding to this notice should submit their capability statement as well as the Buy Indian Act Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form (attached). Consistent with the revised Buy Indian Act, HHS/IHS adopted the definition of an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) set forth in 48 CFR 1480.201. This definition includes the following requirement, amongst others: �the Indians or Indian Tribes must, together, receive at least a majority of the earnings from the contract.� Instructions for submission are outlined further below. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT NAICS Code: 621210 Small Business Size Standard: $9 million in average annual receipts Estimated Period of Performance: Three (3) months from date of award, with a possible option to extend services for up to six (6) months in accordance with FAR 52.217-8, to ensure continuity of care pending award of a planned follow-on long-term contract for the same requirement. Estimated Value: To be determined based on market research. 1. Purpose of Notice This Sources Sought Notice is issued in accordance with the Buy Indian Act, 25 U.S.C. � 47, and its implementing regulations, to conduct market research and determine the availability and interest of qualified Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) capable of providing the supplies/services described below. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submission of information does not guarantee that a solicitation for this requirement will be issued, nor does it obligate the Government to award any resulting contract. 2. Background / Requirement Description The Billings Area Indian Health Service (BAIHS), Blackfeet Service Unit (BFSU), provides comprehensive healthcare services to American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries residing on and near the Blackfeet Indian Reservation in Browning, Montana. The Blackfeet Community Hospital requires continued access to dental oral and maxillofacial surgery services to meet the clinical needs of its patient population. A draft Performance Work Statement is attached to this notice. 3. Anticipated Acquisition Strategy This requirement is subject to the Buy Indian Act order of precedence set forth at HHSAR 326.603-1. Respondents are requested to identify their status as an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) or Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE), if applicable. If the Government determines after market research that there is no reasonable expectation of obtaining two or more competitive offers from ISBEE/IEE concerns, the Contracting Officer may proceed under the deviation process at HHSAR 326.603-3. 4. Indian Economic Enterprise / Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise Requirements To be considered an IEE or ISBEE for purposes of this notice, an entity must meet the applicable definitions and ownership/control requirements set forth at 25 U.S.C. � 47 and HHSAR 326.601, including but not limited to: The combined Indian, Federally Recognized Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Corporation ownership of the enterprise constitutes not less than 51%; The Indian, Federal Recognized Indian Tribes, or Alaska Native Corporations must, together, receive at least 51% of the earnings from the contract; and The management and daily business operations must be controlled by one or more individuals who are Indians. Respondents claiming IEE or ISBEE status should identify their status clearly in their response and be prepared to provide supporting documentation upon request. 5. Information Requested Interested and qualified sources, particularly IEEs and ISBEEs, are requested to submit the following information: Company Information: Name, address, point of contact, phone number, email address, and UEI (Unique Entity Identifier). Business Status: Indicate whether your firm qualifies as an IEE, ISBEE, or other small business concern, and identify the specific socioeconomic certifications held (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB), if any. Capability Statement: A narrative not to exceed ten pages describing your firm's experience performing work of the same or similar scope, complexity and clinical setting as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), including at least two relevant past or current contracts, with the following for each: contract number, customer, dollar value, period of performance, and brief description of work performed. Bonding/Licensing (if applicable): Evidence of any required licenses, certifications, or bonding capacity relevant to the requirement. Teaming/Subcontracting: If your firm intends to team with or subcontract to another entity to meet the requirement, identify the proposed teaming partner(s) and the anticipated division of work. Statement of Interest: A brief statement confirming your firm's interest in and capability to compete for this requirement if a solicitation is issued. 6. Instructions for Submission All responses shall be submitted electronically to Prudence.YellowOwl@ihs.gov no later than September 14, 2026 at 2:30pm MT. Responses shall be limited to 10 pages, in PDF, 12-point font. Responses will not be returned and will not be publicly posted. All information marked as proprietary or confidential will be treated accordingly to the extent permitted by law. 7. Disclaimer This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or to award a contract. No entitlement to compensation shall arise as a result of a firm's submission of information in response to this notice or the Government's use of that information. Firms responding to this notice are solely responsible for all costs associated with their response. The Government reserves the right to consider a non-IEE/ISBEE small business or full-and-open acquisition strategy if market research indicates an insufficient number of interested and qualified IEEs/ISBEEs exist to reasonably expect competition.

This requirement is mandated by MIL-STD-129P referenced under the Preservation, Packing and Marking portion of this TDP. 2-12. 85 Percent SHELF-LIFE REMAINING REQUIREMENT APPLICABLE TO ACQUISITION/PROCUREMENT A. Acquisition/procurement documentation shall specify that shelf-life items/material will have not less than 85 percent (allowing for rounding to whole months) of shelf-life remaining at time of receipt by the first Government activity. Any delivery from a contractor not having at least 85 percent shelf-life remaining shall normally be considered non-conforming. Refer to Appendix E of this Manual to determine the amount of time that 85% equates to in terms of remaining shelf life for Type I or Type II shelf-life codes. B. In supporting imminent use or consumption, the 85% shelf-life remaining on receipt by first Government activity may be modified or adjusted as deemed prudent at the discretion of PMs and IMMs, when support alternative arrangements such as EC, PV, DVD or local purchase are effected. Use of support alternatives for shipment/delivery to storage facilities as stock will conform to the 85% rule. 2-13. CONTRACTOR MARKING. Shelf life items will be marked for identification and control. For Type I shelf life items: apply one, as appropriate; date manufactured, date cured (for elastomeric and rubber products only), date assembled, or date packed (subsistence only); and expiration date. B. For Type II shelf life items: apply one, as appropriate; date manufactured, date cured (for elastomeric and other rubber products only), date assembled, and date packed (subsistence only), and inspect/test date. C. For both Type I and Type II markings in subparagraphs A and B above: the date shall be expressed by the numeric month and the last 2 digits of the calendar year; i.e., 06/95, with the day of that month being the last day. D. Different Dates on Identical Items. When two or more unit packs of identical items bear different dates of manufacture, dates of cure, dates of pack, or dates of assembly, the earliest date shall be shown on the shipping container. E. For Type I drugs and biologicals: the expiration date only is required. The expiration date should be marked in accordance with FED-SPEC PPP C 186 (reference (q)). Manufacturer date shall not be shown for medical items having expiration dates. F. title: Tarjouspyyntö jätteiden keräyksistä ja kuljetuksista Mäntyharjun kunnan alueella
description: Tarjouspyyntö jätteiden keräyksistä ja kuljetuksista Mäntyharjun kunnan alueella Kymenlaakson Jäte Oy:n toimialueella on kolme urakka-aluetta, jotka on jaettu pienempiin osaurakoihin. Mäntyharjun jätteenkuljetusurakka on osa Kymenlaakson Jäte Oy:n jätteenkuljetusurakoita. Mäntyharjun urakka kilpailutetaan yhtenä kokonaisuutena, joten hankintaa ei jaeta osiin. Suunnitellun urakan laajuus on mitoitettu siten, että sen hoitaminen edellyttää arviolta 2-3 jäteautoa. Urakan kokonaisuus soveltuu myös mikro- ja pienyrityksille joko itsenäisesti (tai yhteenliittymänä) toteutettavaksi. Hankintayksikkö on arvioinut hankinnan jakamista osiin hankintalain 75 §:n mukaisesti. Tässä hankinnassa urakan jakaminen ei arvioinnin mukaan lisäisi mikroyritysten osallistumismahdollisuuksia, vaan urakan toteuttaminen yhtenä kokonaisuutena tukee tehokasta reittisuunnittelua, kaluston joustavaa käyttöä ja hallinnollisesti selkeää toteutusta. Tämän arvioidaan edistävän myös pienempien toimijoiden edellytyksiä osallistua kilpailutukseen. Tämä tarjouspyyntö koskee Kymenlaakson Jäte Oy:n (jäljempänä hankintayksikkö) Mäntyharjun kunnan alueella kotitalouksien, vapaa-ajan kiinteistöjen, kunnan hallinto- ja palvelutoiminnan kiinteistöjen sekä muiden asiakkaiksi liittyneiden kiinteistöjen jäteastioiden tyhjennystä, pesuja ja jätteiden kuljetuspalveluiden hankintaa.,

description: SBH | Schulbau Hamburg hat als Landesbetrieb der Freien und Hansestadt Hamburg (nachstehend SBH genannt) die Aufgabe, die Schulimmobilien unter Berücksichtigung der schulischen Belange nach wirtschaftlichen Grundsätzen zu planen, zu bauen, zu unterhalten und zu bewirtschaften und die mehr als 400 Schulen an die Behörde für Schule und Berufsbildung (BSB) zu vermieten. --------------- Für die Klassen-Typengebäude an der Fritz-Schumacher-Schule in Hamburg soll eine serielle energetische Sanierung der Gebäude 02, 03, 04, 05 und 08 durchgeführt werden. Hierbei wird eine neue Gebäudehülle in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise realisiert und der Sanierungsstandard Effizienzhaus 4 EE (KfW 40) wird erreicht. Zudem werden Gründächer mit PV-Anlagen hergestellt und die Umstellung der Wärmeversorgung auf Wärmepumpen inkl. Erneuerung der Heizflächen umgesetzt. Im Innenbereich werden die Garderoben in Differenzierungsflächen umgewandelt und die Sanitärbereiche neu gegliedert. Auf Erdgeschossebene wird pro Haus jeweils ein barrierefreies WC errichtet und allgemeine Barrierefreiheit hergestellt. Im EG wird für jedes Haus zusätzlich eine neue Teeküche eingerichtet. Die Boden- und Deckenbeläge sowie die Elektrik werden erneuert. Für die Sanierung wird der DGNB Gold Standard angestrebt. Vor dem Umbau wird eine Schadstoffsanierung durchgeführt, wobei im Wesentlichen asbesthaltige Wand- und Deckenputze entfernt werden. --------------- Hier: Maurer --------------- Sockeldämmung inkl. Erdarbeiten (950 m), Innendämmung von Kellerdecken (810 m2), Durchbrüche in Mauerwerk, Kleinere Stahlbetonarbeiten (22,7 m3), Innenputzarbeiten (600m2)

title: AMRT Telescoping Mast
description: Product Description TELESCOPING MAST PRODUCT DESCRIPTION The FLNG-CDP requires a life cycle replacement for a critical component of the YF309J, Trailer, Special Purpose-the primary telescopic tower utilized by the Air and Marine Reconnaissance Team (AMRT) during reconnaissance and observation (R&O). AMRT seeks a commercial off the shelf platform that provides next generation command and control (NGC2), on the move (OTM) and at the halt (ATH) capabilities. The desired platform must meet the following capabilities: - Base tube diameter is not more than seven inches. - No more than 6 mast sections. - Retracted height no more than 70 inches, with an extended mast height of 20 feet. - Total mast weight under 205 lbs. - Mast must support 200 lbs. payload. - MIL-STD-810 tested aluminum and stainless-steel construction. - Manual winch with self-lubricating shims. - Upper and lower electro-mechanical safety switches. - Custom mast head adaptor for various sensors. - Cable guide rings on each mast section. - Tool-less accessories to simplify set up and storage. - Extended wall mount to attach mast to Mobile Operations Command Trailer. - Drainage ports.
