title: Turn-key Detention Facilities
description: ----------------Amendment A0002-------------- The government is in receipt of questions from industry and is the process of drafting responses to questions received and revising applicable attachments. A future amendment (A0003) will be issued to incorporate government responses and amended attachments tomorrow, 9/11/26. The purpose of Amendment A0002 is to: 1) Extend proposal submission due date and time to 9/14/26 at 5:00 PM ET. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. ----------------Amendment A0001-------------- The purpose of Amendment A0001 is to: 1) Revise sections of the PWS. See Attachment 01 A0001 - Turnkey Facility PWS (Non-IHSC) (Requirements A- Denver, B -Miami and C-Philadelphia), and Attachment 02 A0001 - Turnkey Facility PWS (IHSC) (Requirement D-Seattle). 2) Add the following attachments: Attachment 15 Turn-key pricing Spreadsheet. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. ----------------------------------------------------------------------- Combined Synopsis/Solicitation The Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Office of Acquisition Management, Detention Compliance and Removals, is issuing Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 70CDCR26R00000026 for multiple turnkey detention facility requirements. ICE intends to award separate single-award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the provision of comprehensive detention facility services, transportation services, food services, operations and maintenance services, and related support services for ICE detainees in Enforcement and Removal Operations custody. The Government may make one or more awards under this solicitation. Each requirement/facility will be evaluated and awarded separately. The anticipated contract type for each requirement is a hybrid Firm-Fixed-Price and Labor-Hour IDIQ contract. Each contract is anticipated to include a 120-month ordering period, inclusive of a 60-day transition period. The Government is also evaluating the option to extend services for up to six months pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The solicitation includes the following requirements/facilities: Requirement A: Denver Area of Responsibility Requirement B: Miami Area of Responsibility Requirement C: Philadelphia Area of Responsibility Requirement D: Seattle Area of Responsibility Requirements A, B, and C are for Non-IHSC-staffed facilities. Requirement D is for an IHSC-staffed facility. Description of Requirement The Contractor shall furnish the proposed detention facility and provide all management, supervision, personnel, labor, equipment, vehicles, supplies, materials, and services necessary to provide safe, secure, humane, and compliant detention services for ICE detainees. Services shall be provided 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year. The required services include, but are not limited to: Turnkey detention facility operations; Secure custody, care, supervision, and safekeeping of detainees; Facility management and administration; Staffing, supervision, training, and quality control; Food service operations; Armed transportation services; On-call guard services; Intake, release, classification, detainee accountability, and detainee property management; Facility security and control operations; Video surveillance and related security systems; Virtual attorney visitation capability and operation; Legal access, law library access, and group legal orientation space; Religious services, recreation, disability accommodations, and language access; Commissary operations; Emergency response, evacuation planning, and continuity of operations; Operations and maintenance, including preventive and corrective maintenance; Fire, life safety, environmental, sanitation, pest control, utility, accessibility, and physical plant compliance; Records management, reporting, data ownership, and information security compliance; Compliance with applicable ICE detention standards, ACA ALDF standards, PREA requirements, and other applicable federal requirements. For Non-IHSC-staffed facilities, the Contractor shall also provide comprehensive health care services in accordance with the applicable Performance Work Statement, facility-specific requirements, ICE detention standards, and related requirements. For the IHSC-staffed facility, ICE Health Services Corps will provide health services, and the Contractor shall provide required facility support, space, security, and related services. The Contractor shall also provide and maintain required ICE, IHSC, OPLA, USCIS, EOIR, and other administrative and support spaces as applicable to the specific requirement and facility-specific addenda. Applicable Standards and Compliance Requirements Performance shall comply with the requirements set forth in the solicitation, Performance Work Statements, facility-specific requirements, and all applicable attachments. These include, but are not limited to: Applicable ICE detention standards; American Correctional Association Adult Local Detention Facility standards; DHS Prison Rape Elimination Act standards; Architectural Barriers Act and Rehabilitation Act requirements; Occupational Safety and Health Administration requirements; Fire, life safety, building, and environmental requirements; DHS and ICE information security, privacy, records, and data protection requirements; Applicable transportation, firearms, body armor, licensing, and credentialing requirements; Applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, except where federal requirements control. The Contractor shall obtain and maintain required permits, licenses, approvals, certifications, inspections, and accreditations necessary for performance. Phase 1 and Phase 2 Evaluation Process The Government intends to conduct this procurement using a multi-phase proposal submission and evaluation process. Phase 1 Phase 1 consists of: Volume I, Administration Volume II, Readiness Screening Phase 1 will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis for each proposed facility. Offerors must receive a Pass for every Phase 1 criterion for a facility in order to advance to Phase 2 for that facility. Phase 1 readiness criteria include: Legal control of the proposed facility; Minimum beds and required configuration; Building, fire, life safety, and occupancy; Zoning, licensing, and local approvals; Staffing pipeline and training readiness; Key leadership and core security/control systems; Transportation assets and equipment; Environmental and site information, including information required to support the Government�s NEPA review. A Phase 1 Pass notice does not constitute award, approval of the proposed facility, an affirmative responsibility determination, or completion of the Government�s NEPA review. Phase 2 Phase 2 consists of: Volume III, Technical Proposal Technical and Management Approach Corporate Experience Volume IV, Price Proposal Only offerors and facilities that receive a Phase 1 Pass will be invited to submit Phase 2 proposals for the applicable facility. Basis for Award For each requirement/facility, the Government intends to award a single-award IDIQ contract to the responsible offeror whose conforming proposal provides the best value to the Government, considering price and non-price factors. This acquisition will use a tradeoff approach and is not a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable acquisition. The Government may select a proposal other than the lowest-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits merit the additional price. The Government may award based on initial proposals without discussions. Offerors are encouraged to submit their best technical and price terms in their initial proposal. Proposal Submission Offerors may propose for one, more than one, or all four requirements/facilities. Offerors submitting proposals for multiple facilities shall provide separately identifiable proposal content for each facility. Information submitted for one facility will not be assumed to apply to another

title: Audio Distribution System for Human Space Flight
description: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) /Johnson Space Center (JSC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for State-of-the-art Audio Distribution Systems with potential to ruggedize for use in Human Spaceflight spacecraft and induced environments. NASA/JSC is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of Small Businesses and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals for Audio Distribution System for Human Spaceflight. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small, 8(a), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Smal Business (SD-VOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) or Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) business set-aside based on responses received. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: 1. SB Subcontracting goals; 2 Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or 3. Strategies to increase SB participation, including: Breaking requirements into smaller components Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches Currently, phase one seeks to identify a commercial audio distribution system that may be ruggedized to operate reliably in human spaceflight environments. Manufacturers of commercial, automotive, aerospace, and military audio communication systems are invited to respond to this request for information on recommended audio systems, subsystems, and software to be considered. Information to be provided includes general functionality, size, weight, power, interfaces, processor platform, reliability features, and other relevant design elements. In phase two, NASA will assess the information received in phase one against spacecraft functional and environmental requirements, as well as the feasibility of any necessary design modifications. Modifications are expected to be necessary to improve reliability and may include electronic circuit re-design, substitution of electronic components with radiation tolerant devices, or enhancements to software development and hardware manufacturing processes to comply with applicable standards. For reference, Appendix A (Attachment I) provides a high-level summary of requirements for a spacecraft audio system. Interested providers may opt to respond to this sources sought with recommendations to deliver full spacecraft audio system hardware and software, an audio subsystem that provides partial functionality, or a software and/or IP core solution to be deployed on other spacecraft avionics hardware. No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. Interested firms are responsible for monitoring this website for the release of any presolicitation or solicitation notice. Vendors having the capabilities necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements are invited to submit appropriate documentation, literature, brochures, and references. All responses must be submitted electronically via email to Contracting Officer, Carlos Roman, Carlos.Roman@nasa.gov and Contract Specialist, Alex Olley, Alex.T.Olley@nasa.gov, no later than September 14, 2026, 4:00 p.m. CDT. Please reference in your communication Titled: Source Sought- 80JSC026ADSHSF - Audio Distribution System for Human Space Flight in any response. This sources sought notice is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Respondents deemed fully qualified will be considered in any resultant solicitation for the requirement. NASA intends to publicize a listing of respondents to facilitate teaming arrangements. Should your firm desire not to be included in this listing, clearly indicate this desire in your response.

description: **Update 9 Sept: Q&A will be posted by COB 10 Sept. Attachment EUS_AOI1_AWACS has been updated. PAE MDS is interested in awarding FAR-based Contract (e.g., FAR Part 12) or Prototype Project Other Transaction Agreement (pOTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Anticipate a 12-month base plus 4 12-month options for this AOI. AOI #1 AWACS leverages the competitive process under DHA Enterprise-Wide Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) HT003826SC005, https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/cd16b90540b7407fb4de1e028cea74d4/view Opportunity Overview: To maximize the value of the Department�s health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unified, outcome-based EUS delivery model. Success in the EUS environment depends on delivering services precisely tailored to diverse user communities. A one-size-fits-all support model is unacceptable. The EUS ecosystem supports 11 distinct User Domains, ranging from point-of-care clinicians in garrison, to operational combat medics in disconnected environments, to the beneficiaries accessing the patient portal, as well as the highly specialized System Administrators, Biomedical Engineers, and local Information Technology (IT) support personnel who maintain these environments. Proposed solutions must demonstrate the flexibility to accommodate the unique workflows, priorities, and connectivity constraints of these diverse groups. This includes the inherent scalability to absorb new federal partners, seamlessly adapt enterprise workflows (e.g., MEPCOM), and tailor enablement materials for diverse components (e.g., National Guard) as the PAE MDS product ecosystem expands. While this AoI supports Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Military Service staff who interact with beneficiaries (the 11th User Domain), this AoI explicitly excludes a request to address direct, patient-facing digital engagement, which is reserved for Pillar 8 and may be addressed in a future AoI. The total EUS ecosystem is structured around eight integrated Service Pillars: Service Desk & Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) Application & Clinical Workflow Support (Focus of this AoI) Enablement & Adoption Services (Focus of this AoI) Disconnected Enabler Change, Communications, & Trust (Focus of this AoI) Service Intelligence & Governance Support Program Management & Service Integration Beneficiary Digital Experience While this specific AoI focuses exclusively on transforming and integrating Pillars 2, 3, and 5, Offerors must understand that these pillars do not operate in a silo. Any IT solution, automated framework, or workflow compliance strategy proposed under this AoI must be designed to seamlessly integrate with the broader EUS ecosystem, specifically, passing data to the enterprise ITSM Service Desk (Pillar 1) and supporting the overarching Government Service Integration and Management (SIAM) processes and integration authorities. title: Audio Distribution System for Human Space Flight
description: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) /Johnson Space Center (JSC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for State-of-the-art Audio Distribution Systems with potential to ruggedize for use in Human Spaceflight spacecraft and induced environments. NASA/JSC is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of Small Businesses and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals for Audio Distribution System for Human Spaceflight. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small, 8(a), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Smal Business (SD-VOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) or Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) business set-aside based on responses received. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: 1. SB Subcontracting goals; 2 Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or 3. Strategies to increase SB participation, including: Breaking requirements into smaller components Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches Currently, phase one seeks to identify a commercial audio distribution system that may be ruggedized to operate reliably in human spaceflight environments. Manufacturers of commercial, automotive, aerospace, and military audio communication systems are invited to respond to this request for information on recommended audio systems, subsystems, and software to be considered. Information to be provided includes general functionality, size, weight, power, interfaces, processor platform, reliability features, and other relevant design elements. In phase two, NASA will assess the information received in phase one against spacecraft functional and environmental requirements, as well as the feasibility of any necessary design modifications. Modifications are expected to be necessary to improve reliability and may include electronic circuit re-design, substitution of electronic components with radiation tolerant devices, or enhancements to software development and hardware manufacturing processes to comply with applicable standards. For reference, Appendix A (Attachment I) provides a high-level summary of requirements for a spacecraft audio system. Interested providers may opt to respond to this sources sought with recommendations to deliver full spacecraft audio system hardware and software, an audio subsystem that provides partial functionality, or a software and/or IP core solution to be deployed on other spacecraft avionics hardware. description: THE UNITED STATES COAST GUARD REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL DIRECT LEASE Part 1: General Information Action Type: Solicitation / Request for Proposal (RFP) Solicitation Number: USCG-SOHV-LEASE-LOUISVILLE-2026 Title: Lease of Office and Special-Use Space in Louisville, KY for USCG Issuing Contracting Office: U.S. Coast Guard, Civil Engineering Unit Cleveland, Real Property Division Response Deadline: Sep 14th, 2026, 4:00 PM ET. Additionally, properties located outside the boundary lines but within a 0.5-mile driving distance of the major roadways identified as the boundary lines will also be considered eligible. All eligible properties must adhere to all local, state, and federal codes, regulations, and standards, including the Architectural Barriers Act Accessibility Standard (ABAAS) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). This procurement will result in a direct Government lease with terms and conditions to be determined. Part 2: Synopsis and Authority The United States Coast Guard (USCG), a component of the Department of Homeland Security, requires office and special-purpose facility space to support the mission in Louisville, KY. The Government intends to award a Direct Lease to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the government. This solicitation is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 15 and 41 CFR 102-73. The resulting lease will be executed under the authority of 14 U.S.C. � 501(e). It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor this posting on SAM.gov for any amendments. Part 3: Government Requirement � Space and Site The proposed property must meet the following minimum requirements. Offerors must provide a detailed response addressing their capability to meet each specification or propose a viable architectural layout that maximizes these functional requirements in a space-efficient footprint. Total Area: Total square footage of 22,000-24,000 Usable Square Feet (USF) under a fully serviced lease structure. General Space: Secured parking for 11 Government vehicles. 28 enclosed offices and 56 open-concept cubicles (48 sq ft). The property must meet, or be capable of being upgraded to meet, Interagency Security Committee (ISC) Facility Security Level 2 (FSL II) standards. Standards available upon request. The property must not be located within a 100-year floodplain as designated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). The Government requires 24/7/365 unrestricted ingress and egress to the leased space, the building, and the secure GOV parking area. Collaborative Spaces: Two (2) Small Conference Rooms (6-9 seats each). One (1) Medium Conference Room (10-13 seats). One (1) Large Conference Room (14-25 seats). Servicing Personnel Check-in/Walk-Up Station. Approx 1200 USF of Administrative Storage areas. Office Equipment and Mail Room areas. A Nursing Mothers Room. Support and Common Areas: General Building Storage, Janitor's Closet, and Trash/Recycling Room. Shipping and Receiving area. Break Room / Lunch Area including refrigerator and kitchenette. Vending Machine Area. Seating and Standing Waiting Area. Commercial/Residential Laundry Room. At least one (1) Unisex restroom, and dedicated Male/Female restrooms equipped with shower facilities. Medical Approx 300 USF for medical examination area and storage. Mission Areas: A floor-to-ceiling partitioned workspace configured with the following dedicated workstation groupings. Workstations sized to a minimum of 96 sq. ft per workstation: Group A Workstations: 6 workstations Group C Workstations: 3 workstations Group D Workstation: 1 workstation Group E Workstation: 1 workstation Situated immediately adjacent to the partitioned workspace, approximately 200 USF of secured-access administrative space and an additional 400 USF secured-access server room. Detailed command center design standards are available upon request. These secure spaces must be supported by dedicated, redundant 24/7 HVAC climate controls and a 24-hour emergency backup power generation system. Roof-mounted marine-grade VHF radio antenna with dedicated weather-sealed conduit and low-loss coaxial cabling routed directly to the command center. The antenna system must be physically and technically scaled to ensure clear, continuous radio communications along the Ohio River from Mile Marker 591 to Mile Marker 608. Note: Terminal radio equipment at the command center will be Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE), provided and installed by the USCG. Part 4: Lease Term and Evaluation Lease Term: The Government is seeking a total lease term of up to twenty (20) years. The proposed lease structure is a one (1) year firm (base) period with nineteen (19) one-year renewal option periods, exercisable at the sole discretion of the Government. Anticipated Lease Start Date: On or about September 2026. The Government's obligation is contingent upon the annual appropriation of funds. Evaluation Criteria: Best Value Tradeoff: The Government will make an award to the responsible offeror whose proposal is determined to provide the best overall value, considering both technical factors and price. Technical factors are equally as important as price. Price: The total evaluated price for the entire 20-year term. Technical Factors (in descending order of importance): Facility Readiness & Existing Infrastructure: Preference for properties requiring minimal Tenant Improvements, demolition, or construction time to meet mission requirements. Site Access & Security: The quality, safety, and security of site ingress/egress, as well as the security of the dedicated Government-Owned Vehicle (GOV) parking and overall site perimeter. Personnel Amenities: Preference for facilities with fitness center and/or proximity to local gymnasiums. Part 5: Proposal Submission Instructions Interested parties must submit a written proposal addressing all requirements herein. The proposal package must include: Property Details: Address, map showing location, and a narrative describing how the property meets all requirements in Part 3. title: F135 Propulsion System Supply Chain Management & Programmatic Support
description: ******************************************************************************** AMENDMENT 01 - NOTICE OF CLOSURE (JUNE 8, 2026) This Sources Sought Notice is hereby amended to correct the administrative error regarding the system response date and to formally close the market research window. The official response deadline is changed to JUNE 8, 2026, and this notice is now CLOSED. The Government is currently evaluating the capability statements received. All other requirements, terms, and conditions of this notice remain unchanged. ******************************************************************************** DESCRIPTION: The Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support � Richmond (DLA WS RIC) issues this Sources Sought for a potential Long-Term Contract (LTC) in coordination with the transition of the management of the F135 Propulsion System Sustainment from the F-35 Joint Program Office (JPO) to DLA. The potential contract is anticipated to have a five-year base and a five-year option (10-year total period of performance). The potential contract is anticipated to be a comprehensive sole-source requirements-type contract with ancillary services, issued as a basic contract for holistic F135 Engine support under the terms and conditions of basic agreement SPE4AX-22-D-0001. It will include both consumable and depot-level repairable (DLR) spare parts, as well as ancillary services such as programmatic supply chain forecasting and management. The current potential material population for programmatic support currently consists of approximately ~435 DLA-managed common NIINs and approximately ~3,500 non-NSN engine components identified as sole source to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for material support. The remaining ~435 items (see attachment) will not be designated as sole source for material support and will likely remain supported through normal routine DLA supply chain channels on independent acquisitions and are only included in this project for the purpose of holistic forecast management. All items will be evaluated on a line-by-line basis. Items identified for competitive sourcing will be removed from the final award population. Additional items may be added in the future in which case amendment(s) may be made to the sources sought notice. DISCLAIMER: THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT SOLELY ON THE BASIS OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT OR TO OTHERWISE PAY FOR THE INFORMATION SOLICITED. This Sources Sought notice is issued for information and planning purposes only, does not constitute a solicitation, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. The Government requires that only non-proprietary information be submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for the use of any proprietary information submitted. Responses to the Sources Sought will not be returned. The responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right to reject, in whole or in part, any contractor's input resulting from this Sources Sought. Based on the information received in response to this notice, the Government may change the initial acquisition strategy. However, the Government is under no obligation to award a contract because of this announcement. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought. Purpose: This agency proposes this Sources Sought as a means of conducting market research to determine if other companies are capable of providing any items or programmatic services that have been determined to be sole source to Pratt & Whitney. Presently, approximately ~3500 of these items are source controlled to Raytheon Technologies, Pratt & Whitney Military Engines (CAGE codes 52661 &/or 77445). The remaining ~435 items are not sole source to Pratt & Whitney and will be considered for this effort for ancillary programmatic/forecasting support (only) and possible �backup� emergency material support yet to be determined. Objective: The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under authority of FAR 6.302-1. Other interested parties may identify their interest and capability to comprehensively support the objectives by responding to this notice. The proposed sole-source LTC letter solicitation and resulting potential award of a sole-source contract will be issued to Raytheon Technologies Corporation, Pratt & Whitney Military Engines, CAGEs 52661/77445. Other interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement as described below. All responses received by the notice response date will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Responses: Responses are required by no later than 06/08/2026. 1. Responses must include the following information: a. Company Name b. Address c. CAGE Code d. Point of Contact e. Phone f. Email g. Web page URL, if available h. Small business type or category you represent, if applicable i. Identify as a U.S. or Foreign Owned Entity j. Indicate whether your interest is as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor 2. Respondents must address: Their capability to comprehensively support the objectives listed above, including direct-to-Global Spares Pool (GSP) logistics. Experience on efforts that are similar in nature and scope (Major 5th-Gen Propulsion Sustainment). Their specific experience with F135 Engine spare parts and non-provisioned material. Their level of access to the proprietary engineering and logistics data, specifically for the ~3,500 non-provisioned items. Their transition and implementation actions and timeframes to successfully execute the anticipated requirements of this acquisition in a rapid manner. Willingness to provide long-term pricing and Certified Cost or Pricing Data in accordance with the Truthful Cost or Pricing Data statute (10 U.S.C. Chapter 271 and 41 U.S.C. Chapter 35), as implemented by FAR Subpart 15.4, for the full term of the potential contract. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: Responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be readable by Adobe Acrobat. Response to this Sources Sought Notice shall be unclassified and not exceed 20 pages in length. Please note, emails containing file types such as .zip, .xlsx, docx, or other macro-enabled extension, may not be delivered to the intended recipient. All responses and questions under this Sources Sought Notice must be transmitted electronically to the Contracting Officer at jennifer.blamy@dla.mil. title: Portfolio Acquisition Executive, Medical Digital Solutions, (PAE MDS) End User Services (EUS) Area of Interest Application, Workflow, Adoption, and Change Support (AWACS)
description: ***Update 10 Sept: Q&A has been provided via excel attachment. No further questions will be considered. Submission Deadline: Whitepapers must be submitted via email to Katelyn O'Connor, katelyn.j.oconnor.civ@health.mil and Jena Bowman, jena.l.bowman.civ@health.mil no later than September 14, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submissions received after this date and time will not be considered. **Update 9 Sept: Q&A will be posted by COB 10 Sept. Attachment EUS_AOI1_AWACS_090926 has been updated. PAE MDS is interested in awarding FAR-based Contract (e.g., FAR Part 12) or Prototype Project Other Transaction Agreement (pOTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Anticipate a 12-month base plus 4 12-month options for this AOI. AOI #1 AWACS leverages the competitive process under DHA Enterprise-Wide Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) HT003826SC005, https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/cd16b90540b7407fb4de1e028cea74d4/view Opportunity Overview: To maximize the value of the Department�s health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unified, outcome-based EUS delivery model. Success in the EUS environment depends on delivering services precisely tailored to diverse user communities. A one-size-fits-all support model is unacceptable. The EUS ecosystem supports 11 distinct User Domains, ranging from point-of-care clinicians in garrison, to operational combat medics in disconnected environments, to the beneficiaries accessing the patient portal, as well as the highly specialized System Administrators, Biomedical Engineers, and local Information Technology (IT) support personnel who maintain these environments. Proposed solutions must demonstrate the flexibility to accommodate the unique workflows, priorities, and connectivity constraints of these diverse groups. This includes the inherent scalability to absorb new federal partners, seamlessly adapt enterprise workflows (e.g., MEPCOM), and tailor enablement materials for diverse components (e.g., National Guard) as the PAE MDS product ecosystem expands. While this AoI supports Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Military Service staff who interact with beneficiaries (the 11th User Domain), this AoI explicitly excludes a request to address direct, patient-facing digital engagement, which is reserved for Pillar 8 and may be addressed in a future AoI. The total EUS ecosystem is structured around eight integrated Service Pillars: Service Desk & Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) Application & Clinical Workflow Support (Focus of this AoI) Enablement & Adoption Services (Focus of this AoI) Disconnected Enabler Change, Communications, & Trust (Focus of this AoI) Service Intelligence & Governance Support Program Management & Service Integration Beneficiary Digital Experience While this specific AoI focuses exclusively on transforming and integrating Pillars 2, 3, and 5, Offerors must understand that these pillars do not operate in a silo. Any IT solution, automated framework, or workflow compliance strategy proposed under this AoI must be designed to seamlessly integrate with the broader EUS ecosystem, specifically, passing data to the enterprise ITSM Service Desk (Pillar 1) and supporting the overarching Government Service Integration and Management (SIAM) processes and integration authorities. Questions: Must be submitted via email to the POCs listed below no later than September 2, 2026, at 11:00 AM EDT. Answers will be posted collectively on SAM.gov no later than close of business (COB) on September 10, 2026. Questions received after September 2, 2026 11:00AM EDT will not be considered. Submission Deadline: Whitepapers must be submitted via email to Katelyn O'Connor, katelyn.j.oconnor.civ@health.mil and Jena Bowman, jena.l.bowman.civ@health.mil no later than September 14, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submissions received after this date and time will not be considered. Cost of Preparation: Per the CSO terms, the Government is not liable for any costs associated with the preparation of materials submitted in response to this AOI. Important Instructions for Interested Parties: Interested parties are strongly encouraged to review the attached documents in their entirety for complete details regarding this opportunity, including submission requirements and other specific instructions.

title: CNF TRAIL BRUSHING
description: CNF TRAIL BRUSHING This is a non-personal services contract for trail brushing for the Forest Service Chugach National Forest (CNF), Alaska. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government. Purpose: The Forest Service is responsible for maintaining healthy, diverse, and productive National Forests. These responsibilities include maintaining trails and managing vegetation growth. The CNF manages over 500 miles of trails, and the trails identified in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) have been designated as current priorities for brushing services. The purpose of this contract is to manage vegetation growth to ensure safe trail conditions and maintain visitor access to National Forest System lands. Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to provide brushing services to multiple trails located within the Chugach National Forest. Services shall include cutting, trimming, and disposing of live and dead brush/slash, logs and debris. All services shall be performed in accordance with (IAW) this PWS, and all applicable local, state, and federal standards, laws, and regulations. Place of Performance: The trails covered under this contract are located within the Seward Ranger District (SRD) and Glacier Ranger District (GRD), Chugach National Forest, Alaska. The closest communities are Moose Pass and Whittier. Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be from Date of Award until 30 November 2027. Contract Type: The Government will award a Firm-Fixed Price, Stand-Alone, Non-Personal Services Contract. Amendment 0001: The solicitation has been amended to provide responses to questions submitted by offerors. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged.

The Government is interested in all businesses to include 8(a), small business and small disadvantaged business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Hubzone, and Women-Owned small business concerns. title: CNF TRAIL BRUSHING
description: CNF TRAIL BRUSHING This is a non-personal services contract for trail brushing for the Forest Service Chugach National Forest (CNF), Alaska. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government. Purpose: The Forest Service is responsible for maintaining healthy, diverse, and productive National Forests. These responsibilities include maintaining trails and managing vegetation growth. The CNF manages over 500 miles of trails, and the trails identified in this Performance Work Statement (PWS) have been designated as current priorities for brushing services. The purpose of this contract is to manage vegetation growth to ensure safe trail conditions and maintain visitor access to National Forest System lands. Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to provide brushing services to multiple trails located within the Chugach National Forest. Services shall include cutting, trimming, and disposing of live and dead brush/slash, logs and debris. All services shall be performed in accordance with (IAW) this PWS, and all applicable local, state, and federal standards, laws, and regulations. Place of Performance: The trails covered under this contract are located within the Seward Ranger District (SRD) and Glacier Ranger District (GRD), Chugach National Forest, Alaska. The closest communities are Moose Pass and Whittier. Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be from Date of Award until 30 November 2027. Contract Type: The Government will award a Firm-Fixed Price, Stand-Alone, Non-Personal Services Contract.

title: The United States Coast Guard is seeking to acquire, via lease, office space within a radius of current location from the Romano Mazzoli Federal Building, 600 Dr. Martin Luther King Place, Louisville, KY 40207-2239.
description: THE UNITED STATES COAST GUARD REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL DIRECT LEASE Part 1: General Information Action Type: Solicitation / Request for Proposal (RFP) Solicitation Number: USCG-SOHV-LEASE-LOUISVILLE-2026 Title: Lease of Office and Special-Use Space in Louisville, KY for USCG Issuing Contracting Office: U.S. Coast Guard, Civil Engineering Unit Cleveland, Real Property Division Response Deadline: Sep 11th, 2026, 4:00 PM ET. NAICS Code: 531120 � Lessors of Nonresidential Buildings Place of Performance / Delineated Area: The Government's current location is the Mazzoli Federal Building, 600 Dr Martin Luther King Jr Pl, Suite 267, Louisville, KY 40202. Proposed properties located entirely within the boundaries of the Delineated Area depicted in Exhibit A (Delineated Area Map) are fully eligible. Additionally, properties located outside the boundary lines but within a 0.5-mile driving distance of the major roadways identified as the boundary lines will also be considered eligible. All eligible properties must adhere to all local, state, and federal codes, regulations, and standards, including the Architectural Barriers Act Accessibility Standard (ABAAS) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). This procurement will result in a direct Government lease with terms and conditions to be determined. Part 2: Synopsis and Authority The United States Coast Guard (USCG), a component of the Department of Homeland Security, requires office and special-purpose facility space to support the mission in Louisville, KY. The Government intends to award a Direct Lease to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the government. This solicitation is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 15 and 41 CFR 102-73. The resulting lease will be executed under the authority of 14 U.S.C. � 501(e). It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor this posting on SAM.gov for any amendments. Part 3: Government Requirement � Space and Site The proposed property must meet the following minimum requirements. Offerors must provide a detailed response addressing their capability to meet each specification or propose a viable architectural layout that maximizes these functional requirements in a space-efficient footprint. Total Area: Total square footage of 22,000-24,000 Usable Square Feet (USF) under a fully serviced lease structure. General Space: Secured parking for 11 Government vehicles. 28 enclosed offices and 56 open-concept cubicles (48 sq ft). The property must meet, or be capable of being upgraded to meet, Interagency Security Committee (ISC) Facility Security Level 2 (FSL II) standards. Standards available upon request. The property must not be located within a 100-year floodplain as designated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). The Government requires 24/7/365 unrestricted ingress and egress to the leased space, the building, and the secure GOV parking area. Collaborative Spaces: Two (2) Small Conference Rooms (6-9 seats each). One (1) Medium Conference Room (10-13 seats). One (1) Large Conference Room (14-25 seats). Servicing Personnel Check-in/Walk-Up Station. Approx 1200 USF of Administrative Storage areas. Office Equipment and Mail Room areas. A Nursing Mothers Room. Support and Common Areas: General Building Storage, Janitor's Closet, and Trash/Recycling Room. Shipping and Receiving area. Break Room / Lunch Area including refrigerator and kitchenette. Vending Machine Area. Seating and Standing Waiting Area. Commercial/Residential Laundry Room. At least one (1) Unisex restroom, and dedicated Male/Female restrooms equipped with shower facilities. Medical Approx 300 USF for medical examination area and storage. Mission Areas: A floor-to-ceiling partitioned workspace configured with the following dedicated workstation groupings. Workstations sized to a minimum of 96 sq. ft per workstation: Group A Workstations: 6 workstations Group C Workstations: 3 workstations Group D Workstation: 1 workstation Group E Workstation: 1 workstation Situated immediately adjacent to the partitioned workspace, approximately 200 USF of secured-access administrative space and an additional 400 USF secured-access server room. Detailed command center design standards are available upon request. These secure spaces must be supported by dedicated, redundant 24/7 HVAC climate controls and a 24-hour emergency backup power generation system. Roof-mounted marine-grade VHF radio antenna with dedicated weather-sealed conduit and low-loss coaxial cabling routed directly to the command center. The antenna system must be physically and technically scaled to ensure clear, continuous radio communications along the Ohio River from Mile Marker 591 to Mile Marker 608. Note: Terminal radio equipment at the command center will be Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE), provided and installed by the USCG. Part 4: Lease Term and Evaluation Lease Term: The Government is seeking a total lease term of up to twenty (20) years. The proposed lease structure is a one (1) year firm (base) period with nineteen (19) one-year renewal option periods, exercisable at the sole discretion of the Government. Anticipated Lease Start Date: On or about September 20th, 2026. The Government's obligation is contingent upon the annual appropriation of funds. Evaluation Criteria: Best Value Tradeoff: The Government will make an award to the responsible offeror whose proposal is determined to provide the best overall value, considering both technical factors and price. Technical factors are equally as important as price. Price: The total evaluated price for the entire 20-year term. Technical Factors (in descending order of importance): Facility Readiness & Existing Infrastructure: Preference for properties requiring minimal Tenant Improvements, demolition, or construction time to meet mission requirements. Site Access & Security: The quality, safety, and security of site ingress/egress, as well as the security of the dedicated Government-Owned Vehicle (GOV) parking and overall site perimeter. Personnel Amenities: Preference for facilities with fitness center and/or proximity to local gymnasiums. Part 5: Proposal Submission Instructions Interested parties must submit a written proposal addressing all requirements herein. The proposal package must include: Property Details: Address, map showing location, and a narrative describing how the property meets all requirements in Part 3. Proof of Ownership/Control: Evidence of property ownership (e.g., deed) or legal authority to offer the space for lease. Floor Plan: A to-scale drawing showing the proposed layout and dimensions. Pricing Proposal: A detailed price quote showing: Shell Rent Operating Costs Tenant Improvements (TI): A detailed estimate of design and construction costs to meet Government specifications, and the proposed Amortization Interest Rate. Total Annual Rent: For the one-year base period. Option Years: Total annual rent for each of the nine (9) option periods. SAM.gov Registration: Proof of active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) including the Unique Entity ID (UEI). Proposals must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer at the email address below. Hard copy submissions will not be accepted. Send Proposals and Inquiries to: Name/Title: Kevin Werthmuller, Real Estate Contracting Officer (RECO) Address: 1240 East Ninth Street, Suite 2179, Cleveland, OH 44199-2060 Email Address: Kevin.j.werthmuller@uscg.mil Exhibit A: (Delineated Area)

title: DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE (DAF) NONAPPROPRIATED FUND INSTRUMENTALITY (NAFI) NEXGEN FOOD SERVICES OPPORTUNITY
description: �This is a nonappropriated fund purchase and it does not obligate appropriated funds of the United States Government. Nonappropriated funds are generated by the military community through the sale of goods and services and the collection of fees and charges for participation in military community programs. This purchase does not involve federal tax dollars.� DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE (DAF) NONAPPROPRIATED FUND INSTRUMENTALITY (NAFI) NEXGEN FOOD SERVICES OPPORTUNITY PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS & INDUSTRY QUESTIONS I. SAM.GOV PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS 1. General Information Document Type: Presolicitation Notice / Synopsis Notice Type: Presolicitation Anticipated Solicitation Number: [To Be Determined] Contracting Office: Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Purchasing Office (AFNAFPO) / Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), San Antonio, Texas. 2. Points of Contact Primary Contracting Officer: Joshua Blalock, NF-V, DAF; Chief, Food Solutions Division, AFSVC/VPF Email: joshua.blalock.5@us.af.mil Office Phone: (380) 456-9979 Secondary: Tekoah Campbell, NF-IV, DAF; Chief, Food Service and Transformation Branch, AFSVC/VPFT Email: tekoah.campbell@us.af.mil Office Phone: (380) 457-1731 3. Description of Requirement The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) has an upcoming requirement for the management, operation, and culinary transformation of food and beverage services under the Department of the Air Force (DAF) NexGen Food Service Program. The program aims to modernize traditional military dining facilities into modern, campus-style dining venues known as Mission Essential Feeding Facilities (MEFF) and Satellite Facilities, supporting single-quarters enlisted personnel on Essential Station Messing (ESM) as well as cash-paying customers. The selected contractor will partner with DAF military culinary personnel to manage high-quality food preparation, serving, menu planning (under Go for Green� and other nutritional standards), preventative facility/equipment maintenance, custodial services, and potential temporary/mobile feeding solutions. 4. Locations of Performance Services will be performed across three primary installations at the following designated facilities: Luke AFB, Arizona: Ray V. Hensman MEFF (Building 545) and T-Bolt Caf� (Building 954) Offutt AFB, Nebraska: Ronald L. King MEFF (Building 324) and NC3 Alert Facility (Building 478) Shaw AFB, South Carolina: Chief Master Sergeant Emerson E. Williams MEFF (Building 417) and Afterburner Grill Satellite Facility (Building 1511) 5. Contract Structure and Anticipated Period of Performance The NAFI intends to award a single contract consisting of a one-year Base Period and two (2) one-year Option Periods. The contract line items (CLINs) are anticipated to utilize a hybrid of contract types to align performance incentives: Core Food Operations (CLIN 0001 series): Cost-Reimbursable (budget-based operations) Primary Performance Outcomes (CLIN 0002 series): Fixed-Price Incentive Firm (FPIF) Secondary Performance Outcomes (CLIN 0003 series): Fixed-Price Incentive Firm (FPIF) Surge (CLIN 0004 series): Time & Materials (T&M) Temporary Feeding (CLIN 0005 series): Time & Materials (T&M) 6. Special Procurement Considerations Site Visits & Conferences: Pre-proposal site visits and conferences are tentatively planned to take place at Luke AFB, Offutt AFB, and Shaw AFB in CY2026 Q4. Oral Presentations: Offerors may be required to participate in oral presentations at the Air Force Services Center in San Antonio, Texas, to demonstrate their capabilities and understanding of the NexGen requirements. II. INDUSTRY FEEDBACK AND CAPABILITY QUESTIONS To help the Air Force refine its solicitation and evaluate industry capability, interested vendors are requested to respond to the following questions. 1. Corporate Capability & Geographically Dispersed Operations Question 1a: Describe your firm's experience in operating campus-style dining services, particularly those utilizing multi-venue concepts, grab-and-go options, and automated/cashless dining environments. Question 1b: Given the requirement to operate across three geographically dispersed locations (Luke AFB, AZ; Offutt AFB, NE; Shaw AFB, SC), describe your proposed corporate-level management and support structure to ensure consistent quality across all bases. Question 1c: What experience does your firm have managing a blended workforce of contractor staff and military/civilian personnel coexisting and collaborating in the same facility? 2. Operational & Facility Maintenance Management Question 2a: Describe your approach to establishing and executing a proactive Operations Preventive Maintenance Plan (OPMP) for food service equipment, including how you coordinate with third-party service providers and track performance against a set budget. Question 2b: Detail your experience in implementing comprehensive Master Cleaning Plans and ensuring compliance with Tri-Service Food Code or USDA sanitary guidelines to consistently achieve "Substantially Compliant" public health inspection ratings. 3. Menu, Nutrition & Technology Integration Question 3a: Describe your capability to develop monthly seasonal menus and costed recipes that comply with DoD Menu Standards (DoDM 13-38.10) and the Go for Green (G4G) program to promote healthy nutritional choices. Question 3b: Describe your experience integrating contractor food procurement and point-of-sale (POS) inventory databases with government IT networks (such as DLA-T STORES or AFSVC POS systems) without requiring manual data entry. 4. Labor, Recruiting & Subcontracting Question 4a: Operating in a military installation environment presents unique recruitment and retention challenges. What strategies does your firm use to maintain a stable, well-trained workforce, and what is your strategy for supplying staffing to meet military backfill requirements? Question 4b: What is your experience subcontracting with AbilityOne (SourceAmerica) agencies for custodial, warewashing, or other support services? 5. Contract Structure, Risk, & Performance Incentives Question 5a: The proposed CLIN structure uses a hybrid of Cost-Reimbursable (Core Operations), Fixed-Price Incentive Firm (Primary & Secondary Performance Outcomes), and Time & Materials (Surge & Temporary Feeding). Do you find this structure feasible, and does it provide adequate commercial incentives? Please explain. Question 5b: The DAF intends to establish a target budget and apply an "at-risk" management fee (e.g., 20% guaranteed, 80% at risk). What are your views on this fee split, and what alternative risk-reward mechanisms would encourage superior performance? Question 5c: Secondary Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) may include Food Waste reduction, Food Cost Ratios, ESM Propensity to Eat, and Program Innovation. Based on your commercial experience, which of these metrics are most effectively used to tie to performance-based incentive payments? 6. Temporary Feeding Solutions Question 6a: Describe your firm's capability to deploy and set up an executable, mobile temporary feeding solution (e.g., Mobile Kitchen Trailer, Containerized Kitchen) within a 30-day window to support all dayparts (breakfast, lunch, dinner, midnight meal). Question 6b: What are the key cost drivers and capacity assumptions (throughput, labor, and packaging) your firm considers when pricing a 30-day temporary feeding plan?

title: Portfolio Acquisition Executive, Medical Digital Solutions, (PAE MDS) End User Services (EUS) Area of Interest Application, Workflow, Adoption, and Change Support (AWACS)
description: PAE MDS is interested in awarding FAR-based Contract (e.g., FAR Part 12) or Prototype Project Other Transaction Agreement (pOTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 4022. Anticipate a 12-month base plus 4 12-month options for this AOI. AOI #1 AWACS leverages the competitive process under DHA Enterprise-Wide Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) HT003826SC005, https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/cd16b90540b7407fb4de1e028cea74d4/view Opportunity Overview: To maximize the value of the Department�s health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unified, outcome-based EUS delivery model. Success in the EUS environment depends on delivering services precisely tailored to diverse user communities. A one-size-fits-all support model is unacceptable. The EUS ecosystem supports 11 distinct User Domains, ranging from point-of-care clinicians in garrison, to operational combat medics in disconnected environments, to the beneficiaries accessing the patient portal, as well as the highly specialized System Administrators, Biomedical Engineers, and local Information Technology (IT) support personnel who maintain these environments. Proposed solutions must demonstrate the flexibility to accommodate the unique workflows, priorities, and connectivity constraints of these diverse groups. This includes the inherent scalability to absorb new federal partners, seamlessly adapt enterprise workflows (e.g., MEPCOM), and tailor enablement materials for diverse components (e.g., National Guard) as the PAE MDS product ecosystem expands. While this AoI supports Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Military Service staff who interact with beneficiaries (the 11th User Domain), this AoI explicitly excludes a request to address direct, patient-facing digital engagement, which is reserved for Pillar 8 and may be addressed in a future AoI. The total EUS ecosystem is structured around eight integrated Service Pillars: Service Desk & Information Technology Service Management (ITSM) Application & Clinical Workflow Support (Focus of this AoI) Enablement & Adoption Services (Focus of this AoI) Disconnected Enabler Change, Communications, & Trust (Focus of this AoI) Service Intelligence & Governance Support Program Management & Service Integration Beneficiary Digital Experience While this specific AoI focuses exclusively on transforming and integrating Pillars 2, 3, and 5, Offerors must understand that these pillars do not operate in a silo. Any IT solution, automated framework, or workflow compliance strategy proposed under this AoI must be designed to seamlessly integrate with the broader EUS ecosystem, specifically, passing data to the enterprise ITSM Service Desk (Pillar 1) and supporting the overarching Government Service Integration and Management (SIAM) processes and integration authorities. title: Non-Research Long-Term Care facility needed for the enrichment and socialization of Non-Human Primate colony
description: Amendment 5 is being issued to incorporate the Q&A that has been deemed to be materially pertinent to the solicitation and all potential offerors along with resulting changes to the solicitation. The due date has been changed from September 11, 2026 to September 14, 2026 and the due time has been changed from 12:00 PM EDT to 5:00 PM EDT. Amendment 4 is being issued to incorporate Q&A and resulting changes to solicitation. There is no change to due date/time. Amendment 3 is being issued to post a revised copy of the solicitation and extend the due date to 12:00 PM EDT on September 11, 2026. Amendment 2 is being issued to post the Q&A and a modified solicitation package. It also extends the due date to July 23, 2026. Amendment 1 is being issued to extend the due date to 07/20/2026. Another amendment will be issued once Q&A and the revised solicitation is ready. The purpose of this acquisition is to secure permanent housing of approximately 130 NHPs and the responsibility for providing them with a safe, compliant, and humane long-term sanctuary with a limited lead time. The contractor shall implement structured social group formation, behavioral rehabilitation, provide comprehensive lifetime care, and have sole custody and ownership for each animal. The overall objective is to ensure the seamless and humane transfer of all CDC animals into naturalistic and enriched environments that support their physical and behavioral health, within facilities that are compliant with standards set by the GFAS and that maintain these animals as set by applicable animal welfare regulations and standards. The facility must be GFAS-accredited and a sanctuary at which no research or breeding will take place. The facility must not buy, sell, or trade animals or sell animal byproducts. Direct public contact should be prohibited. The facility shall also provide species-appropriate habitat and enclosure design that supports the expression of natural behaviors.

description: This announcement is issued on behalf of the Navy Manufacturing Technology (ManTech) Program. title: NOAA: eLearning Assett Library Renewals
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a firm fixed price contract for a Base year plus two (2) Option Years as a 100% Small Business set-aside for the National Weather Srgvice Leadership Academy in Kansas City, MO. The government intends to make an award to the responsive responsible quoter proving the best value in accordance with FAR 12.203 (c)(2). Brand Name Justification: Offerors must provide proof as an eLearning Brothers approved authorized reseller. The eLearning Brothers brand name Authoring Suite-Gold subscription is essential to the requirement and market research indicates similar products do not meet or cannot be modified to meet agency needs. The National Weather Service Office of the Chief Learning Officer (OCLO) uses eLearning Brothers LLC Subscription - Asset Library extensively to create and maintain multiple types of products which support both in class and online class materials for National Weather Service employees. eLearning Brothers LLC Subscription provides a one subscription stop for the photos, illustrations, templates, and pre-made interactions for a variety of eLearning development software including HTML5 based scripts, Articulate, Camtasia, Captivate, and more. There are currently multiple projects completed and/or maintained with the eLearning Brothers LLC Subscription such as New Hire Orientation, M&S course materials, IDSS Boot Camp, IDSS PCUs, Social Sciences, and others. There are currently nine active licenses for eLearning Brothers LLC Subscription - Asset Library that gives our training staff collaborative access to this software that needs to be renewed to continue using the software as there is no other software that meets OCLO specific needs. Not renewing the eLearning Brothers LLC Subscription - Asset Library will result in slowed productivity by the OCLO, delaying delivery of important training to NWS employees. title: CNF INTEGRATED FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEMS
description: CNF INTEGRATED FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEMS This solicitation is to establish a Firm-Fixed Price, Requirements, Non-Personal Services contract to support multiple fire protection systems for the Forest Service, Chugach National Forest (CNF), Southeast Alaska. Purpose: The purpose of this contract is to ensure fire alarm systems (FAS), fire suppression systems (FSS), backflow preventers, and fire extinguishers are fully functional, compliant with National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) and Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requirements, certified, and ready for emergency use. Description of Services: The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, and all other items and non-personal services necessary to support multiple fire protection systems for the Forest Service, Chugach National Forest, located in Southcentral Alaska. Services include, but are not limited to, inspection, testing, certification, maintenance, installation, repair, replacement, and disposal of fire protection systems and equipment to ensure all units remain safe, compliant, and fully operational. Place of Performance: The work shall be performed at multiple CNF facilities located throughout Southcentral Alaska: Girdwood, Seward, and Cordova. The Girdwood and Seward sites are accessible by road, while the Cordova sites are accessible only via airplane and/or ferry. Contract Type: The Government will award a Firm-Fixed Price, Requirements, Non-Personal Services contract with up to a 5-Year Ordering Period. Performance shall be made only as authorized by Task Orders issued IAW the Ordering Clause. Subject to any limitations in the Order Limitations Clause or elsewhere in this contract, the contractor shall furnish to the Government all services specified in the Schedule of Items and called for by orders issued IAW the Ordering Clause.
